section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit on most urban streets in South Carolina when no speed limit is posted?
options: a:25 mph,b:30 mph,c:35 mph,d:40 mph
note: South Carolina sets the default speed limit in urban and business districts at 30 mph when no other limit is posted. Always look for posted signs since specific roads may have different limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under South Carolina's GDL program, at what age can a teenager apply for a beginner's permit?
options: a:14,b:15,c:16,d:15 and a half
note: In South Carolina, teens can apply for a beginner's permit at age 15. They must hold the permit for at least 1 year (180 days minimum practice) and meet supervised driving requirements before obtaining a restricted license.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is true about signaling before turns, lane changes, or pulling from a curb?
options: a:You only need to signal during the maneuver.,b:It is a good driving habit and is required by law.,c:It is only necessary if other vehicles are present.
note: You are legally required to signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb so other road users know your intentions in advance. In many states, including South Carolina, you must signal continuously for at least 100 feet before the maneuver at typical speeds, and longer on higher-speed roads when practical.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the speed limit in most South Carolina school zones?
options: a:15 mph,b:20 mph,c:25 mph,d:30 mph
note: South Carolina school zones have a speed limit of 25 mph when children are present or warning lights are active. Always reduce speed well before entering a school zone and watch for pedestrians near the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In South Carolina, what term is used for the offense of driving while impaired by alcohol?
options: a:DWI (Driving While Intoxicated),b:DUI (Driving Under the Influence),c:OWI (Operating While Intoxicated),d:DUII (Driving Under the Influence of Intoxicants)
note: South Carolina uses the term DUI (Driving Under the Influence) — not DWI. This is state-specific terminology and is directly tested on the SCDMV knowledge exam. The legal BAC threshold is 0.08% for drivers 21 and older.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the legal BAC limit for a driver age 21 or older in South Carolina?
note: A BAC of 0.08% or higher is per se illegal for drivers 21 and older in South Carolina. Commercial drivers face a stricter 0.04% limit. At or above 0.08%, the BAC level alone establishes impairment regardless of how the driver appears.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under South Carolina's zero tolerance law, what BAC level is illegal for a driver under 21?
options: a:Any measurable amount — 0.00%,b:0.02%,c:0.04%,d:0.08%
note: South Carolina's zero tolerance law sets the illegal threshold for drivers under 21 at 0.02% BAC. A driver under 21 with a BAC of 0.02% or higher faces DUI charges and license suspension, even if they do not appear visibly impaired.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: South Carolina's seatbelt law for front-seat occupants uses which enforcement type?
options: a:Secondary enforcement — officers must have another reason to stop the vehicle,b:Primary enforcement — officers can stop a vehicle solely for a seatbelt violation,c:Enforcement only for drivers, not passengers,d:No enforcement — seatbelts are recommended but not required
note: South Carolina uses primary enforcement for front-seat occupants, meaning an officer can stop a vehicle solely for a front-seat seatbelt violation. Back-seat passengers are covered by secondary enforcement. All occupants are required to wear seatbelts.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How long must a South Carolina teen hold a beginner's permit before applying for a restricted license?
options: a:6 months,b:180 days (approximately 6 months),c:1 full year,d:90 days
note: South Carolina requires teens under 18 to hold their beginner's permit for at least 180 days (approximately 6 months) before they can take the road test for a driver's license.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under South Carolina's Move Over law, what must you do when approaching a stopped vehicle with flashing lights on the side of the road?
options: a:Move over only for law enforcement vehicles,b:Slow to 25 mph regardless of posted limit,c:Move one lane away if safe, or slow to a safe speed if a lane change isn't possible,d:Activate your hazard flashers and maintain speed
note: South Carolina's Move Over law requires drivers to move one lane away from any stopped emergency, law enforcement, towing, or highway utility vehicle with flashing lights. If moving over is not safely possible, slow to a safe and reasonable speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the speed limit on most South Carolina rural two-lane roads when no sign is posted?
options: a:45 mph,b:50 mph,c:55 mph,d:60 mph
note: The default speed limit on most South Carolina rural roads is 55 mph when no other limit is posted. Interstate highways have a higher default of 70 mph. Always check for posted signs, especially in areas with frequent intersections or pedestrian activity.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under South Carolina's implied consent law, a driver suspected of DUI who refuses a chemical test will face:
options: a:No penalty — the refusal cannot be used against them,b:A 6-month license suspension for a first offense,c:Only a fine, not a license suspension,d:The same penalties as an actual DUI conviction
note: South Carolina's implied consent law means drivers have agreed to submit to chemical testing by driving on state roads. A first-offense refusal triggers a 6-month license suspension. The refusal can also be mentioned in court proceedings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Texting while driving in South Carolina is:
options: a:Legal unless you are under 18,b:Legal for drivers over 21 only,c:Prohibited for all drivers at all times,d:Legal only when the vehicle is stopped at a traffic signal
note: South Carolina prohibits texting while driving for all drivers of any age. Reading, composing, or sending a text message while operating a vehicle is illegal statewide. Violating this law is a primary offense — officers can stop you for it directly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do before turning right on a red light in South Carolina?
options: a:Slow to 10 mph, then proceed,b:Signal, then proceed without stopping if no traffic is coming,c:Come to a complete stop, yield to all traffic and pedestrians, then proceed if clear,d:Wait for the light to turn green
note: Right turns on red are permitted in South Carolina after a complete stop and yielding to all pedestrians and cross traffic. A 'No Turn on Red' sign overrides this rule. Never make the turn until you have verified the intersection is fully clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving and a school bus ahead activates its flashing red lights and extends its stop arm. You are in the lane directly behind the bus. What must you do?
options: a:Pass carefully on the left if no children are visible,b:Stop at least 20 feet behind the bus and wait,c:Slow to 15 mph and proceed past the bus,d:Stop only if children are actively exiting
note: When a school bus displays flashing red lights and its stop arm extends, drivers must stop at least 20 feet away and wait until the lights stop flashing and the arm retracts. On an undivided two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the recommended following distance in South Carolina under normal driving conditions?
options: a:1 second,b:2 seconds,c:3 seconds,d:4 seconds
note: South Carolina recommends the 3-second rule as the minimum following distance in normal conditions. Pick a fixed landmark — when the vehicle ahead passes it, you should reach it no sooner than 3 seconds. In rain or on slick roads, increase to 4–6 seconds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at a 4-way stop at exactly the same moment as a driver to your left. Who has the right of way?
options: a:You do, because the other driver is to your left,b:The other driver, because you are to their right,c:Whoever signals first has the right of way,d:Neither — both must wait for a traffic officer
note: At a 4-way stop when two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver to the RIGHT has the right of way. If you are to the right of the other driver, you go first. Stated differently: you yield to traffic coming from your RIGHT.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red light at an intersection in South Carolina means:
options: a:Yield to cross traffic, then proceed,b:Slow and proceed with caution,c:Stop completely, yield to all traffic, then proceed when safe,d:The signal is malfunctioning — treat as a green light
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign in South Carolina. Come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians in all directions, yield the right of way, and proceed when safe. This is different from a flashing yellow, which means caution without requiring a full stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a South Carolina highway, you see a solid yellow line on YOUR side of the center stripe. This means:
options: a:You may pass if the road ahead appears clear,b:You are prohibited from crossing the center line to pass,c:Passing is allowed for vehicles going faster than 55 mph,d:You are in a passing zone — proceed when safe
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the road means you may not cross the center line to pass. The solid line indicates a no-passing zone due to limited visibility — a hill, curve, or other hazard. Wait for a dashed yellow line on your side before passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on an interstate in South Carolina. What is the maximum speed limit for passenger vehicles in most rural sections?
options: a:65 mph,b:70 mph,c:75 mph,d:80 mph
note: South Carolina's standard interstate speed limit for passenger vehicles is 70 mph in rural sections. Urban interstate sections through major cities like Columbia or Charleston may have lower posted limits. Always follow the posted sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following actions is NOT allowed when passing another vehicle on a two-lane road in South Carolina?
options: a:Passing when there is a dashed yellow center line on your side,b:Passing on a long, straight section with clear visibility ahead,c:Passing when approaching the crest of a hill where oncoming traffic cannot be seen,d:Passing a slow-moving farm vehicle with adequate sight distance
note: Passing near the crest of a hill is prohibited because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Passing is also prohibited on curves, near intersections, in school zones, and wherever solid yellow lines appear on your side. Visibility must be clear for the entire passing maneuver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: An emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches from the opposite direction on a divided highway. What must you do?
options: a:Pull to the right and stop as soon as safely possible,b:Maintain speed — on a divided highway the rule does not apply to you,c:Slow to 25 mph until the emergency vehicle passes,d:Move to the left lane to create space
note: Even on a divided highway when an emergency vehicle approaches from the opposite direction, South Carolina law requires you to pull to the right and stop. The right-and-stop rule applies regardless of direction on undivided roads; on divided roads local customs may vary, but pulling right and stopping is always safest and required by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What color and shape is a railroad advance warning sign?
options: a:White rectangle with a red R,b:Yellow circle with a large X and 'RR',c:Red octagon with 'STOP',d:Orange diamond with a locomotive symbol
note: Railroad advance warning signs are round (circular), yellow, and display a large X with 'RR' — warning drivers that a railroad crossing is ahead. The circular shape is reserved specifically for railroad warning signs, making them distinctive from other warning signs (which are diamond-shaped).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In South Carolina, when must you turn on your vehicle's headlights?
options: a:Only between midnight and 5 AM,b:Only when it is raining heavily,c:From sunset to sunrise and whenever visibility is reduced to less than 500 feet,d:Only on rural roads and highways
note: South Carolina requires headlights from sunset to sunrise and any time weather reduces visibility to less than 500 feet. Many states also require headlights whenever windshield wipers are in use — a rule that is tested because drivers often forget it applies in light drizzle as well.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are making a left turn at an intersection with a green light. Oncoming traffic is still moving. When can you turn?
options: a:Immediately — a green light gives you the right of way to turn,b:Only after you enter the intersection and oncoming traffic clears,c:After you yield to oncoming traffic and find a safe gap,d:Only when a dedicated left-turn arrow appears
note: A solid green light allows you to turn left, but you must first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians in the crosswalk. Enter the intersection to position yourself, then wait for a safe gap before completing the turn. Failing to yield on a left turn is one of the most common crash causes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A yellow diamond-shaped sign with a pedestrian symbol means:
options: a:No pedestrians allowed on this road,b:A school zone is ahead — reduce speed,c:Pedestrian crossing ahead — be prepared to stop,d:Parking area for pedestrians only
note: A yellow diamond sign with a pedestrian symbol warns drivers of a pedestrian crossing ahead. Reduce speed, scan for people crossing or preparing to cross, and be ready to stop. This type of crossing may or may not have a marked crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under South Carolina law, which of the following is true about nighttime driving restrictions for teens with a restricted license?
options: a:No nighttime restrictions exist in South Carolina,b:Drivers under 16 may not drive between midnight and 6 AM,c:Drivers under 17 may not drive between midnight and 6 AM without a licensed adult,d:Drivers under 18 may not drive at all between 10 PM and 5 AM
note: South Carolina restricts drivers under 17 with a restricted license from driving between midnight and 6 AM unless accompanied by a licensed adult age 21 or older, or driving to/from work or a school-sponsored activity. The curfew is midnight — not 10 PM or 11 PM.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a green traffic signal arrow pointing left indicate?
options: a:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic,b:You may turn left without yielding — oncoming traffic is stopped,c:Left turns are prohibited at this intersection,d:Oncoming traffic has the green — yield before turning
note: A green arrow (protected left turn) means you may turn in the direction of the arrow without yielding — oncoming traffic has a red light. Protected turns are the safest type of left turn. When the arrow ends and a solid green appears, you must then yield to oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving and your wheels drift off the paved road onto a soft shoulder. What is the safest way to return to the pavement?
options: a:Jerk the wheel sharply back onto the road immediately,b:Apply the brakes hard and stop before returning,c:Ease off the gas, steer gently, and gradually return to the lane when safe,d:Continue on the shoulder until you reach a driveway
note: When wheels drift onto a soft shoulder, ease off the gas and steer gently — do not jerk the wheel. Sudden overcorrection causes rollovers, especially at highway speeds. Gradually return to the lane when speed has reduced and you have a clear, safe entry.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an uncontrolled railroad crossing in South Carolina, you must:
options: a:Stop completely regardless of whether a train is visible,b:Slow to 15 mph and check for trains,c:Slow down, look and listen in both directions, and only cross when safe,d:Maintain speed if no warning lights are active
note: At uncontrolled railroad crossings, South Carolina law requires you to slow down, look both ways, and listen for trains before crossing. You are not required to stop unless a train is coming or warning signals are active — but you must be certain the tracks are clear. Trains cannot stop quickly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: South Carolina's Move Over law applies to which types of stopped vehicles with flashing lights?
options: a:Law enforcement vehicles only,b:Law enforcement and fire/rescue vehicles only,c:Emergency, law enforcement, towing, and highway utility vehicles,d:Any vehicle using hazard flashers on the side of the road
note: South Carolina's Move Over law covers emergency vehicles, law enforcement, towing/recovery operations, and highway utility vehicles — any vehicle performing roadside operations with activated warning lights. The law is designed to protect both first responders and service workers operating on or near the roadway.

question: Do drivers need to stop for a stopped school bus when traveling in the opposite direction on a four-lane highway?
options: a:Drivers in the opposite direction must stop unless the highway is physically divided by a median or barrier.,b:Drivers in the opposite direction never have to stop on any four-lane road.
note: Whether you must stop for a school bus depends on whether the roadway is physically divided, not just on the number of lanes. On a four‑lane road with no physical median or barrier, drivers in both directions must stop for a bus with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm. Only on a divided highway, where a median or barrier separates opposing traffic, are drivers traveling in the opposite direction generally not required to stop, though they must slow and use caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with opposing traffic, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:Only after signaling for at least five seconds.,b:When there is enough room between you and the passed vehicle.,c:Immediately regardless of distance.
note: After passing, you should not move back into your lane until you can see the front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror and there is a safe following distance. This ensures you do not cut off the other driver and that you have enough space to slow or react if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you driving too slowly?
options: a:When you are driving slower than 40 mph on any highway.,b:When you block or interfere with vehicles moving at a normal, safe speed for conditions.,c:When you do not pass other cars often.
note: You are driving too slowly when your speed is so low that you block or interfere with vehicles moving at a normal, safe speed for conditions. Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can be just as dangerous as speeding because it causes sudden braking, lane changes, and increases the risk of collisions.

question: What is the only reliable way to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink coffee,b:Exercise,c:Allow your body time to eliminate the alcohol,d:Take a cold shower
note: Only time lowers your BAC. Your body must metabolize the alcohol, and this process cannot be sped up by coffee, exercise, cold showers, or any other trick. You may feel more awake with caffeine or a shower, but your coordination, judgment, and reaction time remain impaired until enough time has passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking facing uphill where there is no curb, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road,b:Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road (right),c:Keep the wheels straight,d:Turn wheels toward the center of the road
note: When parking uphill with no curb, turn the front wheels toward the edge of the road. If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll away from traffic and off the roadway instead of into the lane.

question: When visibility is low because of fog, what is the proper driving technique?
options: a:Turn on interior lights to improve visibility,b:Slow down and use low beam headlights,c:Increase speed to clear the fog quickly,d:Use high beams for better viewing
note: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. If visibility becomes extremely poor, pull completely off the road and wait until conditions improve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your headlights to warn others,b:Reduce speed drastically,c:Check your rearview and side mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind-spot vehicles,d:Turn on your hazard lights
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check your rearview and side mirrors, and then look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Only move when you are sure the lane is clear and you have enough space.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Apply the brakes hard,b:Stay off the brakes and steer to regain control,c:Pump the brakes repeatedly,d:Turn off the engine immediately
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, avoid braking hard. Sudden or hard braking can make the skid worse. Instead, ease off the accelerator and steer smoothly in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. In vehicles without ABS, you may need to pump the brakes gently; with ABS, apply firm, steady pressure and let the system work.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on an interstate and you intend to change lanes or pass, what should you do?
options: a:Always use cruise control before changing lanes.,b:Stop on the shoulder first if tired.,c:Signal before changing lanes or passing and make sure the lane is clear.
note: Before changing lanes or passing on an interstate, always signal to let other drivers know your intentions, then check your mirrors and blind spots and move only when it is safe. Never stop on the shoulder unless it is an emergency.

question: What can happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of both may be reduced,b:The combined effects of both substances may be increased,c:Nothing will happen,d:They cancel each other out
note: Mixing alcohol with other drugs is dangerous because the substances can interact and intensify each other’s effects. This can greatly increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, impair judgment, and raise the risk of overdose or a crash. You should never assume another drug will cancel out alcohol; they often make impairment worse.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and make a U-turn on the highway.,b:Back up to the missed exit.,c:Roll down your window and ask for directions.,d:Continue to the next exit and return safely.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, keep going to the next exit, then safely turn around or follow signs to return. Never stop, back up, or make a U-turn on the highway, as this can cause serious crashes with fast-moving traffic.

question: What must you do when you approach a stopped school bus on your side of a two-lane road with red lights flashing?
options: a:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,b:Stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing.,c:Slow down to 10 mph and pass carefully.
note: On a two-lane road, when a school bus on your side has red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. Passing at any reduced speed is illegal and extremely dangerous because children may be crossing the road.

question: If your vehicle has a mechanical problem, what is the safest action?
options: a:Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road when possible.,b:Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.,c:Signal and pull into the slow lane and stop there.
note: If your vehicle has a mechanical problem, signal, turn on your hazard lights, and carefully move off the roadway to the shoulder or a safe area away from traffic. Stopping in a travel lane is very dangerous because other drivers may not see you or have time to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you treat an intersection where the traffic signal is not operating?
options: a:Proceed without stopping if the intersection looks clear.,b:Only stop if police are present.,c:Drive quickly through to avoid delays.,d:As an all-way stop: come to a full stop and yield before entering.
note: When a traffic signal is completely out, you must treat the intersection as an all-way stop. Come to a full stop, then proceed in turn, yielding to any vehicles already in the intersection and to pedestrians. Driving through without stopping is unsafe and against the law.

question: When sharing the road with a truck, what should you remember about trucks' stopping ability?
options: a:They have a smaller turning radius than passenger cars,b:They can stop as quickly as motorcycles,c:They require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles,d:They require less distance to stop than smaller vehicles
note: Trucks are much heavier than passenger cars, so they need more distance to come to a complete stop, even with good brakes. When following or cutting in front of a truck, leave extra space so the driver has enough room to stop safely if traffic slows or an emergency occurs.

question: If you experience a tire blowout while driving, which of the following steps are appropriate?
options: a:Immediately stop in the middle of the road,b:Accelerate to maintain control,c:Turn sharply to reach the shoulder quickly,d:Remove your foot from the gas and do not immediately apply the brakes
note: If a tire blows out, take your foot off the accelerator, steer straight, slow gradually, and then pull off the road.

question: A large truck ahead is making a right turn on a street with two lanes in each direction. What is likely to occur?
options: a:The truck must remain in the right lane the entire turn.,b:The truck will always use the left lane to turn.,c:The truck may need to swing wide to finish the turn.,d:The truck can finish the turn in either lane.
note: Large trucks often need extra room to turn right because their rear wheels follow a tighter path than the front wheels. To avoid hitting the curb, parked cars, or pedestrians, the truck may swing wide to the left before completing the right turn. Give trucks plenty of space and never try to squeeze between a turning truck and the curb.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate and swerve back immediately.,b:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.,c:Slow down gradually and carefully steer back onto the road when it is safe.,d:Stop on the shoulder and remain there indefinitely.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and slow down gradually while keeping the vehicle straight. Do not jerk the wheel or brake hard. When you have slowed and it is safe, gently steer back onto the roadway, checking traffic before re-entering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you use your turn signal?
options: a:Only when changing lanes.,b:Whenever you intend to turn or move left or right, including changing lanes and entering or leaving traffic.,c:Only when pulling away from the curb.
note: You must use your turn signal any time you intend to move left or right, not just for lane changes. This includes turning at intersections, changing lanes, entering or leaving a parking space, pulling away from or toward the curb, and entering traffic from a driveway or alley. Signaling lets other road users anticipate your actions and helps prevent collisions.

question: True or False: By driving in South Carolina, you have consented to submit to chemical tests for intoxication if requested by law enforcement.
options: a:Only if arrested,b:False,c:True,d:Only if under 21
note: South Carolina, like all states, has an implied consent law. By driving on public roads, you agree in advance that if an officer lawfully requests a chemical test (such as a breath, blood, or urine test) after a DUI arrest or lawful stop, you will submit to it. Refusal can lead to license suspension and other penalties, even if you are not ultimately convicted of DUI.

question: If your vehicle lacks ABS and you need to stop quickly, what is the recommended technique?
options: a:Hold the brake pedal down hard and steer.,b:Lightly tap the brakes repeatedly.,c:Firmly pump your brakes.
note: In a vehicle without ABS, you should use a firm pumping action on the brake pedal in an emergency stop. Press the brakes firmly until the wheels almost lock, then release slightly and reapply. This helps you slow quickly while still being able to steer. In a vehicle with ABS, you press and hold the brake pedal firmly and let the system pump for you.

question: What color and text style do temporary construction and maintenance signs use?
options: a:Red background with green writing.,b:Green background with white writing.,c:Yellow background with blue writing.,d:Orange background with black writing.
note: Temporary construction and maintenance (work zone) signs are standardized with an orange background and black symbols or lettering. The bright orange color alerts drivers to changing road conditions, workers, lane shifts, or reduced speeds so they can slow down and proceed with extra caution.

question: When following a motorcycle, what should you do?
options: a:Share the same following distance as behind cars always.,b:Follow closer because motorcycles stop faster.,c:Assume motorcyclists are more visible than cars.,d:Allow extra space in front of your vehicle.
note: When following a motorcycle, increase your following distance. Motorcycles can stop and maneuver more quickly than larger vehicles and are harder to see. Leaving extra space gives you more time to react if the rider slows, swerves, or stops suddenly, reducing the risk of rear‑end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn from a one-way street, which lane should you be in?
options: a:The lane nearest the center of the street.,b:The lane nearest the right curb.,c:Any available lane.,d:The lane nearest the left curb.
note: When turning left from a one‑way street, you should start from the lane nearest the left curb. Begin and end your turn in the proper lane so you stay in your lane and avoid conflicts with traffic going straight or turning right. Always signal and check mirrors and blind spots before turning.

question: Which action disrupts smooth traffic flow?
options: a:Slowing down to look at a crash or unusual scene.,b:Avoiding needless lane changes.,c:Using public transit instead of driving.,d:Maintaining a steady speed with traffic.
note: Slowing down just to look at a crash or unusual scene (rubbernecking) causes sudden speed changes, backups, and can trigger rear‑end collisions. Safe drivers keep their attention on the road and maintain a steady speed with traffic instead of slowing to look.

question: What do double solid yellow lines painted down the middle of the road mean?
options: a:Railroad crossing ahead.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction,c:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,d:Only passing by heavy trucks allowed.
note: Double solid yellow center lines mean vehicles in both directions may not cross the lines to pass. You may usually cross them only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road, or when directed by traffic control, but not for passing another moving vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is illegal and may result in fines and/or imprisonment?
options: a:Participating in or assisting a race on a public highway.,b:Speeding.,c:Driving barefoot.,d:Steering with one hand.
note: Organizing, participating in, or assisting in a speed contest or race on a public road is illegal in all states and can lead to fines, license suspension, and even jail time. While speeding is also illegal, the question specifically refers to conduct that commonly carries the possibility of imprisonment, which clearly applies to illegal racing.

question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light you may:
options: a:No longer turn under any circumstance.,b:Still turn in the arrow's direction but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:Have the right-of-way over oncoming traffic.,d:Only go straight.
note: A green arrow gives you a protected turn, but when it changes to a solid green light, you may still turn in that direction only after yielding to oncoming traffic, bicycles, and pedestrians in the crosswalk. You no longer have a protected turn and must wait for a safe gap.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following best describes a safe place to pass another vehicle?
options: a:On a hill or curve where visibility is limited.,b:At any railroad crossing.,c:At a street crossing or highway intersection.,d:Only where you can see far enough ahead to be sure no oncoming traffic is present.
note: Passing is only safe and legal where you have a clear view far enough ahead to be sure no oncoming traffic or hazards are present. You must never pass on hills, curves, at intersections, railroad crossings, or anywhere signs or road markings prohibit passing.

question: If a transit vehicle signals to re-enter the roadway after a stop, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to the transit vehicle and allow it to re-enter.,b:Honk to alert the driver.,c:Speed up to pass before it merges.,d:Remain in your lane and ignore its signals.
note: When a bus or other transit vehicle signals that it is pulling away from a stop, you must yield and allow it to re-enter traffic when it is safe. This often means slowing down or changing lanes so the large vehicle can merge smoothly and safely.

question: When entering a gap in highway traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up and force other vehicles to make way.,b:Check traffic ahead, behind, and in the lane you’re entering,c:Stop in the lane until a gap appears.,d:Watch only the cars behind the gap.
note: When entering a gap in highway traffic, you must be sure the space is safe. Check the traffic ahead of you and behind you, and also check the traffic in the lane you are entering, including your blind spots. Never force your way in or stop in a moving lane; instead, adjust your speed smoothly to fit into the gap.

question: What does a solid white edge line that slants left toward the center of the road indicate?
options: a:The road narrows ahead (edge line angles into the roadway).,b:There is an intersection ahead.,c:You must turn left soon.,d:There is a passing zone ahead.
note: A solid white edge line marks the outer edge of the roadway. When this line angles or slants toward the center of the road, it warns that the usable roadway is narrowing ahead, so you should be prepared to adjust your position and speed.

question: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on water; how can you reduce the chance of hydroplaning?
options: a:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.,b:Put on cruise control to keep a constant speed.,c:Slow down.,d:Drive faster to get through the water quickly.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose contact with the road and ride on a thin layer of water, usually at higher speeds on wet pavement. The best way to reduce the chance of hydroplaning is to slow down in wet conditions and make smooth steering and braking inputs so your tires can maintain traction.

question: At a crosswalk, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Construction workers must yield to vehicles,b:Pedestrians must be yielded to by vehicles,c:Only pedestrians with signals have the right-of-way,d:Pedestrians must yield to vehicles
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks, whether the crosswalk is marked or unmarked, unless a traffic signal or police officer clearly directs otherwise. Always be prepared to stop for people crossing the street at intersections and marked crosswalks.

question: When you approach an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe,b:Slow down and proceed with caution,c:Stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red,d:Only stop if other vehicles are present
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield the right‑of‑way as needed, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: True or false: You do not have to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights if it is on a private road.
options: a:True.,b:Only if the bus is on a driveway.,c:Only for commercial vehicles.,d:False.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must stop whether it is on a public street or a private road, unless a specific state exception applies (such as on the opposite side of a divided highway). Treat private roads and parking lots the same as public roads for school‑bus stopping rules.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about making a right turn is correct?
options: a:You should turn from the rightmost lane and enter the rightmost lane unless signs or markings allow otherwise.,b:You should not swing wide to the left when making a right turn.,c:You may make a right turn on red after stopping and yielding, unless prohibited by a sign.,d:You must always wait for a green light to turn right, even if there is no traffic.
note: After yielding to traffic and pedestrians, you may turn right on red unless a sign specifically prohibits it; stay close to the right curb and turn into the nearest lane.

question: If another vehicle suddenly cuts directly in front of you creating a hazard, what should you do first?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas pedal to increase your following distance.,b:Swerve immediately into the adjacent lane without checking.,c:Honk and slam on the brakes as your first reaction.,d:Speed up to pass the vehicle that cut in front of you.
note: If a vehicle pulls in too closely ahead of you, the safest first response is to ease off the accelerator to increase your following distance. This gives you more time and space to react. Only brake hard or swerve if you cannot avoid a collision by simply slowing and creating space.

question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:The condition of the pavement.,b:The condition of your brakes and tires.,c:The vehicle's speed.,d:All of the above.
note: Braking distance is affected by several factors: your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road surface. Higher speeds greatly increase the distance needed to stop, and worn brakes, bald tires, or wet/icy pavement will also lengthen braking distance.

question: Fatigue while driving increases the risk of:
options: a:Being on time.,b:Missing an exit only.,c:Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
note: Fatigue slows your thinking and reaction time and can cause you to fall asleep at the wheel. A drowsy driver may drift out of their lane or fail to react to hazards, greatly increasing the risk of a serious crash.

question: When the driver behind you wants to pass, what is the recommended response?
options: a:Maintain the same speed regardless.,b:Speed up to prevent the pass.,c:Slow down to allow room in front of your vehicle for the other driver to complete the pass.
note: When someone wants to pass you, help them do it safely. Slightly reduce your speed to create more space in front of you so the passing driver has room to move back into the lane without cutting too closely in front of you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a crowded freeway, what steps should you take to merge?
options: a:Use the acceleration lane to match freeway speed, use mirrors, check blind spots, and yield to traffic.,b:Stop on the ramp and wait for a large gap.,c:Merge at a much slower speed than traffic.,d:Assume freeway traffic will yield to you.
note: Freeway traffic has the right of way. Use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic, check your mirrors and blind spots, and merge only when there is a safe gap. Do not stop on the ramp unless absolutely necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, what is the appropriate driver response?
options: a:Maintain your speed and proceed.,b:Always come to a complete stop regardless of other vehicles.,c:Yield to any vehicle approaching from the right and be prepared to stop to avoid a crash.
note: At an intersection with no signs or signals, you must yield to vehicles that arrive from your right. Approach slowly, be ready to stop, and proceed only when you are sure it is safe and you will not cause other drivers to brake suddenly.

question: How should you respond to an emergency vehicle with flashing lights in your area?
options: a:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.,b:Stop your vehicle and block its passage.,c:Speed up to avoid the vehicle.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and/or siren, you must yield the right of way. Safely move to the right side of the road and stop if possible, or otherwise create a clear path so the emergency vehicle can pass quickly and safely.

question: Which statement about stopping for school buses is correct?
options: a:You only need to stop for a school bus if you see children crossing.,b:You must stop for a stopped school bus with flashing red lights on any two-lane highway.,c:You must stop for a bus that is completely off the roadway in a passenger loading zone.
note: On a two‑lane road, traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, because children may be crossing the road. You do not have to stop for a bus that is completely off the roadway in a designated loading zone where children are not allowed to cross the street, unless your state law specifically requires it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a road with two or more lanes going the same direction, where should slower traffic generally travel?
options: a:In the left lane except to pass.,b:In any lane.,c:In the right lane except to pass.
note: On roads with two or more lanes in the same direction, slower traffic should usually travel in the right lane so faster vehicles can pass on the left. Staying right unless passing helps traffic flow smoothly and reduces lane‑changing conflicts.

question: What is the best way to prevent a dangerous situation while driving?
options: a:Turn off the radio.,b:Constantly be aware of what is happening around your vehicle.,c:Keep your eyes focused only on the road ahead.
note: The best way to avoid dangerous situations is to stay constantly aware of traffic and road conditions all around your vehicle—ahead, to the sides, and behind. This continuous scanning lets you spot hazards early and gives you more time and space to react safely.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out, what is the best immediate response?
options: a:Pull over immediately without slowing.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly.,c:Apply the brake hard and hold it down.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle going straight. Ease off the accelerator and let the car slow down gradually; brake gently only after you have the vehicle under control and your speed has dropped. Then move off the road to a safe place. Slamming on the brakes can cause a loss of control.

question: Which action will sober someone who has been drinking?
options: a:Getting fresh air,b:Drinking hot coffee,c:Drinking tomato juice,d:Allowing time for the body to eliminate the alcohol
note: Only time allows your body to eliminate alcohol and lower your blood alcohol concentration. Fresh air, coffee, cold showers, or juices may make someone feel more awake, but they do not speed up the liver’s ability to process alcohol or make a person sober.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why should you look farther ahead on a freeway compared to a city street?
options: a:To see potential hazards earlier and allow more time to react.,b:Because it takes a quarter-mile to stop your vehicle.,c:To help you keep up with traffic.
note: On freeways you travel at higher speeds, so you cover more distance in less time. Looking farther ahead gives you more time to see hazards, slow traffic, and merging vehicles early so you can change lanes or adjust speed smoothly instead of braking hard at the last second.

question: For quick, controlled turns, where should your hands be placed on the steering wheel?
options: a:Both hands on the shifter,b:On opposite sides of the steering wheel,c:One on top and one on the bottom,d:Next to each other on the top of the wheel
note: Keeping your hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel (commonly around the 9 and 3 o’clock positions) gives you the best leverage and control. This position allows quick, precise steering movements while keeping the vehicle stable during sudden turns or evasive maneuvers.

question: Which driving abilities are reduced by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Alertness and concentration.,b:Reaction time and coordination.,c:All of the above.,d:Only night vision.
note: Alcohol and many drugs slow brain function and muscle coordination. They reduce alertness and concentration and increase reaction time, making it harder to notice hazards and respond in time. Because they affect multiple skills at once, all of the listed abilities are impaired.

question: How should you respond when you see a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog at the edge of the roadway?
options: a:Sound your horn to warn them,b:Stop and remain stopped until the person is safely away from the roadway,c:Wave them across the street,d:Slowly drive around them
note: A pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog is visually impaired and has the right‑of‑way. You must stop and remain stopped, giving them plenty of time and space to cross or move away from the roadway safely. Do not honk, wave, or drive around them, as this can confuse or endanger them.

question: Which action typically leads to hydroplaning?
options: a:Frequent sudden turns on dry roads.,b:Sudden stops on dry pavement.,c:Excessive speed on wet pavement.
note: Hydroplaning happens when a layer of water builds up between your tires and the road so the tires lose direct contact. This is most likely at higher speeds on wet pavement, especially with worn tires. Slowing down in rain and driving with good tires greatly reduces the risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a motorist makes a left turn at an intersection, they should yield to a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction:
options: a:Only at marked bike lanes.,b:False.,c:True.,d:Only if the bicyclist is on the sidewalk.
note: When turning left, you must yield to all oncoming traffic that is close enough to be a hazard, including bicyclists. Bicycles on the roadway have the same right‑of‑way as other vehicles, whether or not there is a bike lane or sidewalk involved.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parked facing uphill on a street with a curb, how should you set your wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels slightly to the left,b:Keep the wheels straight,c:Turn the wheels toward the curb,d:Turn the wheels away from the curb
note: When parking facing uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb. If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll back slightly and the front tire will rest against the curb, helping prevent it from rolling into traffic.

question: True or False: In foggy conditions you should use your low beam headlights.
options: a:Only use parking lights,b:Only use high beams,c:TRUE,d:FALSE
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back at you, making it harder to see. Low beams help you see the road and help others see you without creating glare.

question: When weather suddenly changes, what should you do?
options: a:Be especially aware of vehicles behind you and adjust for their speed.,b:Adapt your driving to the new weather conditions.,c:Slow down when driving in rain or fog.
note: When the weather changes suddenly, you must adjust your driving to match the new conditions. This can include slowing down, increasing following distance, turning on appropriate lights, and being especially alert to other vehicles around you.

question: When is it important to reduce your speed?
options: a:Only when other vehicles are speeding.,b:Only on downhill grades.,c:On narrow or winding roads
note: You should reduce speed on narrow or winding roads because your view of oncoming traffic, pedestrians, and obstacles is limited and curves can reduce traction. Slowing down gives you more time to react and helps keep your vehicle under control.

question: If you turn onto a two-lane road divided by a broken yellow line, what does that tell you about the road?
options: a:You are on a one-way street.,b:The road is under repair.,c:Traffic is moving in both directions (two-way road).
note: A broken yellow centerline means traffic flows in both directions and passing is allowed when it is safe and legal to do so. Yellow lines always separate opposite directions of travel, while white lines separate traffic moving in the same direction.

question: If you are already in an intersection when a green light changes to yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately in the intersection,b:Continue and clear the intersection safely,c:Increase your speed to exit the intersection faster,d:Back up to avoid blocking traffic
note: If the light turns yellow after you have entered the intersection, you should continue through and clear the intersection safely. Stopping in the middle of the intersection or backing up is dangerous and illegal in most situations.

question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings you should always:
options: a:Trust stopped vehicles and pass cautiously.,b:Only check the road ahead.,c:Slowly pass vehicles that are stopped for no reason.,d:Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
note: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, always look to both sides as well as ahead to see pedestrians, cyclists, and other vehicles that may be entering your path. Never assume stopped vehicles can be safely passed; they may be yielding to someone you cannot see.

question: Which statement about blind spots is true?
options: a:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,b:You can check blind spots using only your rearview mirrors.,c:Having one outside mirror on each side eliminates blind spots.
note: Large trucks and buses have much larger blind spots than passenger cars, especially directly behind them and along both sides. Even with properly adjusted mirrors, every vehicle has blind spots, so you must turn your head to check them before changing lanes. Do not linger alongside large trucks where the driver may not see you.

question: Which is NOT a factor used to determine stopping distance?
options: a:Perception time,b:Reaction distance,c:Braking distance,d:Steering ability
note: Total stopping distance is the sum of perception time (seeing the hazard), reaction distance (moving your foot to the brake), and braking distance (the distance the vehicle travels while slowing to a stop). Steering ability does not change how far it takes you to stop in a straight line.

question: If your car begins to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?
options: a:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.,b:In the opposite direction of the skid.,c:Keep the wheels straight and do not turn.
note: When a car begins to skid, you should look and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. This helps the tires regain traction and keeps you from overcorrecting. As the vehicle starts to straighten out, gently adjust the steering as needed and avoid sudden braking or jerky movements.

question: In bad weather you should:
options: a:Brake hard to stop faster.,b:Steer off the road immediately.,c:Steer and brake smoothly.,d:Drive in a low gear at all times.
note: In bad weather, the road surface is more slippery and it is easier to lose control. Steer and brake smoothly so your tires can maintain traction. Sudden hard braking or sharp steering can cause skids or loss of control, especially on wet, icy, or snowy roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you use a freeway exit ramp correctly?
options: a:Slow down once you are on the exit ramp.,b:Begin slowing only after you have come to a complete stop on the shoulder.,c:Keep the same freeway speed all the way through the exit ramp.
note: When leaving a freeway, signal and move into the exit lane at freeway speed, then slow down only after you are fully on the exit ramp. Braking while still in the main travel lane can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear‑end collision. Use the ramp area to reduce speed to the posted advisory speed for the exit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who is required to wear seat belts in a moving vehicle?
options: a:Only front-seat occupants and required child passengers.,b:Only the driver and children under 18.,c:All occupants of the vehicle should be properly restrained.
note: Everyone in a moving vehicle should wear a seat belt or appropriate child restraint. Seat belts greatly reduce the risk of serious injury or death in a crash by keeping occupants from being thrown around inside the vehicle or ejected. Many states legally require all occupants to be properly restrained, and at minimum all front‑seat occupants and children must be buckled up.

question: When you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, what must you do?
options: a:Change lanes and maintain your speed,b:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead and slow down,c:Ignore them if traffic is light,d:Speed up to get through the work zone quickly
note: Orange signs and cones indicate a work zone. You must slow down, be prepared to stop, and watch for workers, lane shifts, and construction equipment. Work zones often have reduced speed limits and narrowed lanes, so extra caution and lower speeds help protect both workers and drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a right turn on red (where permitted), you must:
options: a:Slow down and proceed without stopping if the way is clear.,b:Increase your speed because you have the right-of-way.,c:Come to a complete stop
note: Unless a sign says “No Turn on Red,” you may turn right on red only after coming to a complete stop, checking for and yielding to pedestrians and all cross traffic, and then proceeding when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you proceed through an intersection with a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After stopping at least 20 feet back from the intersection.,b:After coming to a complete stop before entering and verifying it is safe.,c:Only if no other vehicles are visible.,d:After slowing down but not stopping.
note: At a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk, you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection, then move forward only when you have checked in all directions and it is clearly safe to proceed.

question: Why should you allow an extra cushion of space behind a vehicle that cannot see its rear?
options: a:Drivers of large vehicles or those towing may not see vehicles directly behind them, so give extra following space.,b:Small passenger cars always stop faster.,c:Station wagons require more space than trucks.,d:It is safe to tailgate them to increase visibility.
note: Large vehicles and vehicles towing trailers often have large blind spots directly behind them. If you follow too closely, the driver may not see you and you will have less time to react. Leave extra following distance so you stay visible and have more space to stop or maneuver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when passing another vehicle?
options: a:Speed up and pass without checking mirrors or blind spots.,b:Check mirrors and blind spots, signal, and pass only when safe.,c:Honk repeatedly while passing.,d:Re-enter your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror with safe space ahead.
note: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots, signal, and make sure you have enough clear space to pass safely. After passing, return to your lane only when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and there is plenty of space between you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you are approaching a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause a conflict.,b:Always come to a complete stop even if the way is clear.,c:Yield only to vehicles on your right.
note: A yield sign means you must slow down and be prepared to stop. You must let traffic and pedestrians already in or close to the intersection go first, and you may proceed only when you can enter without forcing others to slow or stop suddenly.

question: Which sign of an aggressive driver might you observe?
options: a:Using turn signals consistently,b:Erratic,c:Driving slowly and yielding often,d:Pulling over to help other drivers
note: Erratic driving—such as sudden lane changes, tailgating, speeding, or frequent braking—is a common sign of aggressive driving. When you see this behavior, do not engage; instead, create space and let the aggressive driver go ahead.

question: Do bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicle drivers on public roads?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Bicyclists using public roads generally have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers of motor vehicles. They must obey traffic signals, signs, lane markings, and right‑of‑way rules, and motorists must treat them as legitimate road users.

question: True or false: Drivers are always required to stop for a stopped school bus when traveling on a two-lane road.
options: a:True.,b:False.,c:Only during school hours.,d:Only if children are visible.
note: On a two‑lane road with no physical divider, drivers in both directions must stop for a school bus with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended while it is loading or unloading children. You must remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.

question: When steering, how should you hold the wheel and turn it?
options: a:Grasp the wheel tightly with your palms and thumbs tucked inside.,b:Use only your fingertips on the inside of the wheel.,c:Place both hands on opposite sides of the wheel with a firm, relaxed grip, keeping thumbs on the outside of the rim
note: Keep both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel with a firm but relaxed grip, using your fingers and keeping your thumbs on the outside of the rim. This gives you better control and reduces the chance of injury from airbag deployment compared with gripping tightly or wrapping your thumbs inside the wheel.

question: If a cyclist is ahead in your lane and you want to pass, what should you do?
options: a:Pass the cyclist only when you can leave plenty of space, usually by moving into the next lane when it is safe.,b:Tap your horn loudly to make them move over.,c:Wait until the opposite lane is clear and change lanes to pass,d:Follow closely until the cyclist pulls off the road
note: Bicycles are vehicles, but you must give them extra space. Do not squeeze past a cyclist in the same lane. Wait until the opposite lane is clear, then change lanes or move over far enough to leave a safe buffer—at least several feet—before passing, and return to your lane only when you are well ahead.

question: When a stop line is present at an intersection, where must drivers stop?
options: a:Before reaching the stop line.,b:On top of the stop line.,c:Only if pedestrians are in the crosswalk.,d:Past the stop line to improve visibility.
note: At a stop sign with a marked stop line, you must bring your vehicle to a complete stop before the line. Stopping on or past the line can put you into the crosswalk or intersection and endanger pedestrians or cross traffic. After stopping at the line, you may move forward slowly if needed to improve visibility, but the legal stop must be made before the line.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic is merging into your lane on the freeway, what should you do when possible?
options: a:Hold your lane and refuse to change position.,b:Assert your right-of-way by maintaining speed.,c:Make room for merging vehicles.
note: On freeways, drivers already in the through lane should, when safe, help merging traffic by adjusting speed or changing lanes to create a gap. This smooths traffic flow and reduces the risk of collisions at merge points. You still have the right-of-way, but cooperation and making room when possible is the safest practice.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing that lacks flashing signals or gates, what should you do?
options: a:Always stop before crossing the tracks.,b:Cross immediately as quickly as possible.,c:Prepare to yield to any train at the crossing and ensure there is room to fully clear the tracks.
note: At a railroad crossing without gates or flashing lights, you must slow, look, and listen for trains and be prepared to stop. Only proceed when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space on the far side to clear the tracks completely. Never stop on the tracks, and avoid shifting gears while crossing so you do not stall.

question: What problems do worn or bald tires create?
options: a:They improve fuel economy.,b:They prevent hydroplaning.,c:They have no effect on handling.,d:They can increase stopping distance and make turns more difficult.
note: Worn or bald tires have reduced tread, which greatly lowers traction. This increases your stopping distance, makes steering and cornering less stable, and raises the risk of skidding or hydroplaning on wet roads. Keeping tires in good condition is essential for safe braking and control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is true about passing procedure?
options: a:You only need to signal if another car is present.,b:Never check your blind spot when passing.,c:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes and check mirrors and blind spots.,d:You can pass without signaling if on a clear road.
note: Before passing or changing lanes, you must signal in advance (at least 100 feet in most areas), check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Signaling lets other drivers know your intentions, and checking blind spots ensures there is no vehicle hidden beside you before you move.

question: Which activities can cause distracted driving?
options: a:Eating, using a cellphone, or changing the radio.,b:Only texting on a phone.,c:Driving without sunglasses.,d:Listening to the radio at low volume.
note: Distracted driving is anything that takes your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off driving. Eating, using a cellphone, or changing the radio all create this kind of distraction and increase crash risk.

question: To improve visibility in rain or fog, which lights should drivers use?
options: a:Parking lights only.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: In rain or fog, always use low beam headlights. Low beams light the road without bouncing as much light back at you, while high beams can reflect off moisture in the air and actually make it harder to see.

question: Why should you not use high beam headlights in fog or mist?
options: a:It drains the battery faster.,b:Vehicles behind you will follow too closely.,c:The light will reflect back into your eyes and reduce visibility.,d:Other drivers may not see you.
note: High beams shine more light straight ahead and will reflect off fog, mist, or heavy rain back into your eyes. This glare reduces how far and how clearly you can see, so you should use low beams in these conditions.

question: What do two solid yellow lines on the pavement mean?
options: a:Passing is allowed if you are near the top of a hill,b:You may cross to pass if you signal,c:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions,d:Passing is not allowed
note: Two solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean that passing is not allowed for vehicles traveling in either direction. You may only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe and legal, but not to pass another vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you park downhill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn toward oncoming traffic.,b:Toward the side of the road (right),c:Toward the center of the road (left),d:Keep them straight ahead
note: When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the side of the road. If the vehicle rolls, it will move off the roadway instead of into traffic, reducing the chance of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, what checks should you make?
options: a:Only check the inside rearview mirror.,b:Flash your headlights to alert other drivers.,c:Check side mirrors and look over your shoulder to ensure the lane is clear.,d:Immediately slow down without checking.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then quickly look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This ensures there is no vehicle, motorcycle, bicycle, or other hazard in the lane you want to enter before you move over.

question: When driving in areas where children may be present, what should you expect?
options: a:Children will only cross at marked crosswalks.,b:Children will always wait at the curb before crossing.,c:Children will avoid residential streets.,d:Children may run into the street without looking
note: In areas where children may be present—such as neighborhoods, school zones, and parks—you must expect that children can act unpredictably and may suddenly run into the street without looking. Slow down, cover the brake, and be ready to stop at all times in these areas.

question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Yield only to traffic on the left.,d:Continue at normal speed without looking.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. Look carefully for cross traffic, pedestrians, and other hazards, and continue only when it is safe to do so; you do not have to stop unless needed for safety.

question: What color lines divide lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
options: a:Yellow lines.,b:White lines.,c:Red lines.
note: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. Broken white lines mean you may change lanes when it is safe, while solid white lines discourage or prohibit lane changes. Yellow lines are used to separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A prudent driver should:
options: a:Assume most drivers obey right-of-way rules.,b:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.,c:Assume all other drivers obey right-of-way rules.,d:Never yield even if it prevents a crash.
note: Right-of-way rules indicate who should go first, but they do not give anyone an absolute right to proceed regardless of safety. A prudent driver is always prepared to yield the right-of-way if it will help prevent a collision, even when they are legally entitled to go.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The space needed to cross traffic safely depends on which factors?
options: a:Road and weather conditions and oncoming traffic.,b:Only the presence of a stop sign.,c:Only your use of turn signals.
note: The time and space you need to cross traffic safely depend on how fast other vehicles are coming, how far away they are, and how road and weather conditions affect traction and visibility. You must judge the speed and distance of oncoming traffic and allow extra space when roads are wet, icy, or visibility is reduced.

question: Which of these commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Driving well below the flow of traffic.,b:Following other vehicles at a safe distance.,c:Inattentive driving.
note: Inattentive or distracted driving is one of the most common causes of crashes because drivers may miss signals, brake lights, or hazards. Safe following distance and driving with the flow of traffic (within the speed limit) help prevent collisions, while inattention greatly increases risk.

question: Which of the following can lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) and reduce alcohol's effects?
options: a:Drinking coffee.,b:Eating high-fat foods.,c:Taking a cold shower.,d:Time.
note: Only time lowers your blood alcohol concentration. Your body must metabolize the alcohol, and this process cannot be sped up by coffee, food, showers, or any other tricks. You may feel more awake with coffee or a cold shower, but you will still be impaired until enough time has passed for your body to eliminate the alcohol.

question: If there are two railroad tracks side by side, what should you do after one train passes?
options: a:Look and listen for another train on the other track before crossing,b:Drive around lowered gates if the first train has passed,c:Always assume it's safe to cross after the first train,d:Speed up to get across quickly
note: When there are multiple railroad tracks, one train passing does not mean it is safe to cross. Another train may be coming on the other track, sometimes hidden by the first train. After one train passes, stay behind the gates if they are still down and continue to look and listen carefully for another train before crossing.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow signal mean?
options: a:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light and indicates you should prepare to stop.,b:It always allows turns in the indicated direction.,c:It is not used on traffic signals.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turning phase is ending. You should slow down and prepare to stop if it is safe to do so, just as you would for a circular yellow light. If you are already in the intersection when the yellow arrow appears, complete your turn with caution.

question: When you see a sign for your chosen exit, how should you respond?
options: a:Signal and move into the exit lane promptly,b:Reduce your speed once you are within the deceleration lane,c:Both signal and move into the lane and then slow to the posted exit speed,d:Ignore the sign until the last moment
note: When you see the sign for your exit, signal early, check traffic, and move smoothly into the exit or deceleration lane. Once you are in that lane, gradually reduce your speed to match the posted exit speed. Do not slow sharply while still in the main travel lane, as that can surprise drivers behind you.

question: How can you ensure your physical condition won't impair your driving?
options: a:Have regular physical exams, know medication effects on driving, and drive within your limitations.,b:Ignore physical issues while driving.,c:Only avoid driving if you feel extremely ill.,d:Assume all medications are safe to take before driving.
note: Safe driving requires that you are physically and mentally fit to drive. Regular checkups help you know your limitations, and you must understand how any medications you take can affect alertness, vision, or reaction time. If your condition or medication could impair you, you should not drive or should limit your driving accordingly.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and indicates that passing on the left is allowed when it is safe. You may cross the line to pass if you have enough clear distance ahead and no oncoming traffic or other hazards. If conditions are not safe, you must stay in your lane even though passing is permitted.

question: When a traffic signal turns green, what is your responsibility?
options: a:Honk before entering the intersection,b:Back up if someone is blocking you,c:Accelerate as quickly as possible,d:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic still in the intersection
note: A green light means you may go if the intersection is clear, but it does not give you the right to move immediately without checking. You must first yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in the intersection that are completing their movements. Enter only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle in which situations?
options: a:Only at flashing yellow lights.,b:Only at intersections with stop signs.,c:At a stop sign,d:Only when pedestrians are present.
note: You must come to a complete stop at a stop sign before the crosswalk, stop line, or entering the intersection, and remain stopped until it is safe to proceed. In addition, the law also requires you to stop for steady or flashing red traffic signals and whenever directed by a traffic officer or flagger.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb (left) and set the parking brake.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb (right).
note: When you park facing uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb and let the vehicle roll back slightly until the tire gently touches the curb. If your brakes fail, the curb will stop the car from rolling into traffic. Always set the parking brake as well.

question: Before switching on the ignition, what safety step should you take?
options: a:Confirm that only adult passengers have buckled their belts.,b:Only buckle child passengers' belts.,c:Buckle your safety belt and make sure passengers have buckled theirs.
note: Before starting the car, buckle your own safety belt and make sure every passenger, adults and children, is properly buckled. The driver is responsible for ensuring that all occupants are using seat belts or appropriate child restraints.

question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light and have not yet entered. What should you do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light,b:Come to a safe stop if you can do so,c:Sound your horn and proceed,d:Continue through without slowing
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection, you should slow down and stop if you can do so safely. Only continue through if you are too close to stop safely when the light turns yellow.

question: A motorist must stop for a school bus unloading children on a two-lane road:
options: a:Only if the bus is in your lane.,b:Only if children are on the roadway.,c:True.,d:False.
note: On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing to load or unload children. You must remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the bus moves or the driver signals you to proceed.

question: What is the term for slowing down to look at collisions or unusual events, and why avoid it?
options: a:Rubbernecking; it causes traffic congestion.,b:Alert driving; it prevents collisions.,c:Defensive driving; it improves safety.,d:Sightseeing; it reduces delays.
note: Rubbernecking is when drivers slow down just to look at a crash or something unusual on the road. This unnecessary slowing disrupts traffic flow, increases congestion, and can lead to rear-end and secondary collisions. Keep your attention on the road and maintain a safe, steady speed.

question: To avoid glare from oncoming headlights at night, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your high beams at them,b:Glance briefly toward the right edge of the road,c:Stare at the bright lights to adjust faster,d:Keep focus on the centerline
note: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night, briefly look toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide, rather than staring into the lights. This helps protect your night vision while still keeping you oriented on the roadway.

question: A steady green arrow at an intersection generally allows drivers to:
options: a:Ignore the arrow if the circular light is red.,b:Merge into any lane in the arrow's direction without yielding.,c:Reverse direction.,d:Turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to traffic and pedestrians.
note: A steady green arrow means you may make the protected turn in the direction of the arrow. Even though opposing traffic is stopped, you must still watch for and yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and any vehicles already in the intersection.

question: A driver signaling with the left arm bent upward is indicating they intend to:
options: a:Stop.,b:Turn right.,c:Slow down.,d:Turn left.
note: Standard hand signals use the left arm: straight out for a left turn, bent upward for a right turn, and bent downward for slowing or stopping. A left arm bent upward clearly indicates the driver intends to turn right.

question: Why must drivers be particularly alert for motorcycles?
options: a:Motorcyclists are less skilled drivers than other motorists.,b:Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see than cars.,c:Motorcycles rarely use their headlights.
