note: Drivers must be especially alert for motorcycles because they are smaller, can be easily hidden in blind spots, and are harder to see in traffic. Their size also makes it more difficult to judge their speed and distance, so extra caution and careful scanning are essential.

question: On which surfaces does your vehicle's stopping distance increase?
options: a:On wet or icy roads.,b:On paved highways in good condition.,c:Only when driving at night.
note: Stopping distance increases on wet, icy, or otherwise slippery surfaces because your tires have less traction. It takes longer for the brakes to slow the vehicle, so you must allow more following distance and reduce speed in these conditions.

question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Treat it as a yield signal and continue,b:Come to a full stop,c:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly,d:Slow down and proceed with caution
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to any traffic or pedestrians with the right of way, and then proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe.

question: When driving through work zones, you should:
options: a:Maintain your normal speed through the zone.,b:Change lanes frequently.,c:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop.,d:Increase your speed to clear the zone quickly.
note: In work zones you must slow down, obey the posted work-zone speed limits, and be prepared to stop suddenly. Workers, equipment, and lane shifts can appear unexpectedly, so extra caution and reduced speed are required.

question: Does the presence of double solid yellow lines in the center of the road allow passing from either direction?
options: a:Yes,b:No,c:No, they prohibit passing from either direction,d:No, you must stay in your lane at all times
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit crossing the centerline for passing in either direction, except to turn into driveways or entrances.

question: As daylight begins to fade, which lights should you use to help others see your vehicle?
options: a:Emergency flashers.,b:Parking lights.,c:Low beam headlights.,d:High beam headlights.
note: As it starts to get dark, turn on your low-beam headlights so other drivers can see you and you can see the road better. Parking lights alone are not enough while driving, and high beams should be reserved for dark, open roads with no oncoming traffic or vehicles ahead.

question: What does defensive driving involve?
options: a:Identifying dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents,b:Racing to avoid being cut off by other drivers,c:Following the vehicle ahead closely to reduce reaction time,d:Ignoring other drivers' errors
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning for potential hazards, predicting what other road users might do, and adjusting your speed and position early to avoid conflicts. The goal is to prevent collisions rather than just reacting at the last moment.

question: Which of these is a prohibited parking location?
options: a:Within 100 feet of a driveway.,b:Within 45 feet of a fire hydrant.,c:On a sidewalk.
note: Parking on a sidewalk is prohibited because it blocks pedestrians and can force them into traffic. You also may not park within a short distance of fire hydrants (commonly 15 feet) or block driveways, since emergency access and property access must be kept clear.

question: Are the effects of alcohol on reflexes and judgment dependent on the type of alcoholic beverage?
options: a:Effects are most pronounced with mixed drinks.,b:Effects are less pronounced with beer than wine.,c:Effects are less pronounced with wine than beer.,d:Effects depend on how much alcohol is in the bloodstream.
note: The effect of alcohol on your reflexes and judgment depends on your blood alcohol concentration (BAC), not on whether you drank beer, wine, or liquor. A standard serving of each type of drink can contain about the same amount of alcohol, so impairment is determined by how much alcohol is in your bloodstream, how quickly you drank it, your body size, and other factors.

question: When is parking on the shoulder of a freeway allowed?
options: a:If you need to look at a map for directions.,b:Only in an emergency; otherwise parking on the shoulder is prohibited.,c:As long as you turn on your hazard lights.
note: You may stop or park on the shoulder of a freeway only in an emergency, such as a breakdown or medical issue. For non‑emergencies, you must continue to the next exit or safe area off the freeway. If you must stop for an emergency, pull as far off the roadway as possible and turn on your hazard lights so other drivers can see you.

question: How should you check for vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Rely on the inside rearview mirror.,b:Use your horn to detect vehicles.,c:Look over your shoulder into the appropriate blind spot.,d:Only use the outside rearview mirrors.
note: Blind spots are areas alongside and slightly behind your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors. Before changing lanes or merging, quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to make sure no vehicle is in your blind spot.

question: As a pedestrian, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Entering a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.,b:Using crosswalks when vehicles are present.,c:Waiting for vehicles to stop before crossing.,d:Using sidewalks when available.
note: As a pedestrian, you should never step into a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching and may not have enough time or distance to stop safely. Even if you have the right‑of‑way, you must make sure it is safe to cross and that drivers see you and are stopping.

question: If your accelerator becomes stuck while driving, which is the best immediate action among these?
options: a:Slam on the brakes hard.,b:Turn on your hazard lights as you take steps to safely stop the engine and slow down.,c:Blow your horn to warn others.
note: If your accelerator sticks, keep control of the vehicle and focus on slowing and stopping safely. Turn on your hazard lights to warn others, shift to neutral if you can, apply the brakes firmly but smoothly, and steer to a safe location. Once you are out of traffic and stopped, turn off the engine. Sounding the horn is less important than immediately working to slow and stop the vehicle safely.

question: When making a left turn at an intersection, must you yield to an oncoming bicyclist?
options: a:False — bicycles must yield.,b:Only if the bicyclist is on the sidewalk.,c:Only if the bicyclist is wearing a helmet.,d:True — yield to oncoming bicycles in the same way as vehicles.
note: You must treat bicycles as vehicles when you are turning. When making a left turn, you must yield to oncoming bicyclists in the same way you yield to oncoming cars or motorcycles. If the bicyclist is approaching from the opposite direction and going straight, allow them to pass through the intersection before you turn.

question: You should never park a vehicle in which of the following locations?
options: a:Within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.,b:Within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.,c:Within 30 feet of a traffic signal or flashing beacon on the side of the roadway.,d:All of the above.
note: Parking is prohibited within 50 feet of a railroad crossing, within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection, and within 30 feet of a signal light, stop sign, or flashing beacon on the side of the road. All of these distances help keep sight lines clear so drivers, pedestrians, and train operators can see each other in time to react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the traffic light changes from green to solid yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Stop before entering if you can do so safely; if not, continue through cautiously.,b:Consider it the same as a caution sign and continue without slowing.,c:Stop immediately no matter how close you are.
note: A solid yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when the light turns yellow, continue through the intersection with caution rather than braking suddenly and risking a rear‑end collision.

question: True or false: When making an emergency roadside stop it is unnecessary to set your parking brake.
options: a:False.,b:True.,c:Only if on a flat surface.,d:Only if your vehicle has automatic transmission.
note: When you make an emergency roadside stop, you should secure your vehicle so it cannot roll. Turn on your emergency flashers and set the parking brake, even if the road seems flat or you have an automatic transmission. This reduces the risk of your vehicle moving unexpectedly and improves safety for you and other road users.

question: If you see a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane who is crossing the road, what must you do?
options: a:Pass close to them to move quickly,b:Always yield the right-of-way to that pedestrian,c:Only yield if they are at a corner,d:Tell them the best place to cross
note: Blind or visually impaired pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog have the right-of-way. You must always stop or yield to them and allow them to completely cross safely before proceeding. Never try to hurry past, direct them, or interfere with their movement.

question: What is the recommended habit for checking blind spots when changing lanes or merging?
options: a:Check blind spots only when driving fast.,b:Turn your head to check over your shoulder to see the blind spot.,c:Rely only on side and rearview mirrors.
note: Mirrors do not show areas directly alongside and slightly behind your vehicle, known as blind spots. Before changing lanes, merging, or pulling away from the curb, you must quickly turn your head and look over your shoulder to check these blind spots, in addition to using your mirrors.

question: For drivers aged 21 and older, at what BAC is it illegal to drive?
options: a:0.08 percent or higher.,b:0.05 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: In most U.S. states, for drivers 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher. You can still be impaired at lower levels, but 0.08% is the standard per se legal limit for DUI for adults.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should your car be positioned?
options: a:In the right lane of the one-way street.,b:In the center of the street.,c:In the left lane of the one-way street.
note: When turning left onto a one-way street, finish the turn in the lane closest to the one you left, typically the left lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should you stop at a stop sign that does not have a marked crosswalk?
options: a:Before entering the intersection.,b:At the center of the intersection.,c:After you begin to enter the intersection if nothing is visible.
note: At a stop sign with no stop line or marked crosswalk, you must stop before entering the intersection. Stop where you can see cross traffic, but before crossing the edge of the intersecting roadway, and then proceed only when it is safe and after yielding as required.

question: You must yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog:
options: a:Only at marked crosswalks.,b:At all times.,c:Only when a crossing guard is present.,d:Only if accompanied by another adult.
note: Pedestrians who are blind or visually impaired and using a white cane or guide dog have the right‑of‑way at all times. You must stop and allow them to cross safely, whether or not there is a marked crosswalk, signal, or crossing guard.

question: Which action can reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Allow extra travel time and be patient.,b:Speed up to keep up with traffic.,c:Ignore turn signals from others.
note: Allowing extra travel time helps you stay calm, avoid rushing, and reduces the urge to speed, tailgate, or make aggressive maneuvers. Planning ahead and being patient are key strategies to prevent road rage and keep driving decisions safe and courteous.

question: If you approach a flashing red traffic signal, what is the correct action?
options: a:Treat it as a stop sign and come to a complete stop,b:Proceed without stopping if no vehicles are near,c:Wait until it turns green before moving,d:Slow down but do not stop
note: A flashing red signal is treated exactly like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield the right‑of‑way as needed, and proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is correct?
options: a:It is illegal to go around lowered gates, and you must obey stop signals and flaggers.,b:You may go around gates if you do not see a train.,c:All railroad crossings have flashing lights and gates.
note: At railroad crossings, you must always obey warning lights, bells, signs, gates, and any flagger instructions. It is illegal and extremely dangerous to drive around or under lowered gates, even if you do not see a train, and some crossings have only signs without active signals, so you must approach every crossing with caution.

question: True or false: Alcohol is the single greatest common factor in fatal motor vehicle crashes.
options: a:Only on weekends.,b:Only for drivers under 25.,c:False.,d:True.
note: Alcohol is a major contributing factor in fatal crashes because it slows reaction time, reduces coordination, and impairs judgment and vision. Even small amounts of alcohol can significantly increase crash risk, which is why laws and safety messages strongly emphasize never driving after drinking.

question: How are bicycles treated when used on roadways?
options: a:Bicycles are hazards and may be ignored.,b:Bicycles are considered vehicles and must follow the same road rules.,c:Bicycles must always use sidewalks.,d:Bicycles are not subject to traffic signals.
note: Bicycles are vehicles on the roadway and bicyclists and motorists must follow the same traffic laws.

question: If your wheels slip off the edge of the roadway, what is the correct action to take?
options: a:Slow down and regain control, then gently steer back onto the pavement when safe.,b:Slam on the brakes immediately,c:Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement,d:Speed up and swerve back onto the pavement quickly
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, keep a firm grip on the wheel, ease off the gas, and slow down gradually. Do not slam on the brakes or jerk the steering wheel, because sudden moves can cause you to lose control or skid into oncoming traffic. Once you have slowed and the way is clear, gently steer back onto the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning right on a green light, what must you do?
options: a:Maintain your normal driving speed without yielding.,b:Stop completely before turning even if clear.,c:Sound your horn to warn pedestrians.,d:Yield to pedestrians and any traffic in the intersection.
note: You may turn on steady green unless prohibited, but you must yield to pedestrians and other traffic in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Always come to a complete stop even if the way is clear.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop; yield the right-of-way to cross traffic and pedestrians close enough to be a hazard.,c:Yield only to vehicles on your right.
note: At a yield sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop. Give the right-of-way to any vehicle or pedestrian close enough to enter your path and create a hazard. If traffic is clear, you do not have to stop, but you must enter the intersection only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must you treat a flashing red traffic signal when approaching an intersection?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic, then proceed when safe.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Stop and remain stopped as long as the light is flashing red.
note: A flashing red signal is treated like a stop sign: stop completely, yield to others, and go when clear.

question: Any amount of alcohol in your bloodstream can affect your:
options: a:Knowledge only.,b:Judgment and physical coordination.,c:Vehicle registration status.,d:Right-of-way privileges.
note: Any amount of alcohol can slow your brain’s processing, weaken judgment, and reduce coordination. Even if you are below the legal BAC limit, your ability to react, make safe decisions, and control the vehicle can be impaired.

question: A driving distraction is defined as what?
options: a:Anything that improves your attention to driving,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to the road,d:A device that only affects passengers
note: A driving distraction is anything that takes your attention away from the driving task. This includes visual distractions (eyes off the road), manual distractions (hands off the wheel), and cognitive distractions (mind off driving), all of which increase crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left from a two-way street you should position your vehicle:
options: a:In any lane that is free.,b:Well left of the centerline.,c:Near the centerline.,d:Near the right-hand side.
note: For a left turn from a two‑way street, you should be in the lane closest to the centerline. Position your vehicle near the centerline, signal, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and then turn into the first legal lane without cutting across extra lanes.

question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Only when entering a highway,b:Whenever other drivers are passing you,c:Only when a police officer is present,d:Whenever road or weather conditions make driving unsafe at the posted speed
note: You must adjust your speed to match conditions, even if that means driving below the posted limit. Slow down when visibility is reduced, roads are wet, icy, or gravel, traffic is heavy, or there are hazards such as sharp curves or work zones. The key is to drive at a speed that is safe and reasonable for current conditions, not only when conditions are less than perfect.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your driving lane?
options: a:When the other driver waves you back.,b:After signaling for one second.,c:When someone in the other car honks.,d:When you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing, you need enough space before moving back into your lane. A good rule is to wait until you can see the front of the passed vehicle, including both headlights, in your inside rearview mirror. This shows you have a safe following distance before returning.

question: Should you use high beam headlights when driving in fog?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams, along with fog lights if your vehicle has them, help you see the road and help others see you without creating glare.

question: If a police officer stops you, what is the correct immediate action?
options: a:Speed up to get to a safer location,b:Drive to the nearest police station instead of stopping,c:Exit your vehicle and approach the officer,d:Pull over to the right side of the road and stop as far off the roadway as possible
note: When an officer signals you to stop, slow down and pull over to the right side of the road as soon as it is safe, stopping as far off the roadway as you reasonably can. Stay in your vehicle with your hands visible and follow the officer’s instructions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If several vehicles arrive simultaneously at an uncontrolled intersection, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Yield to the vehicle on your right.,b:Wait until there are no vehicles before proceeding.,c:Yield to the vehicle on your left.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two or more vehicles arrive at the same time, you must yield to the vehicle on your right. This rule helps decide who goes first when there are no signs, signals, or clear right-of-way markings.

question: How many days do you have to notify SCDMV of a name or address change?
options: a:10 days.,b:15 days.,c:30 days.,d:45 days.
note: South Carolina law requires you to notify the SCDMV of any change of name or address within 10 days. Reporting changes promptly helps ensure your license and registration information are accurate and that you receive important notices.

question: In rainy weather you should be most careful when turning or stopping:
options: a:One half hour after it stops raining.,b:After it has been raining all day.,c:During the first half hour of rain.,d:Only during heavy storms.
note: Roads are most slippery during the first 15–30 minutes of rain because oil and other residues on the road surface mix with the water and rise to the top. During this time, be especially careful when turning or stopping, and reduce your speed to maintain traction.

question: Which statements about large trucks are true?
options: a:It is safe to tailgate trucks.,b:Trucks have smaller blind spots than cars.,c:Always drive beside a large truck for better visibility.,d:Trucks have larger blind spots than passenger vehicles and you should avoid driving beside them for long periods.
note: Trucks are much larger than passenger vehicles and have bigger blind spots, especially along the sides and directly behind the trailer. If you drive beside or close behind a truck, the driver may not see you, and the truck may need extra room to turn or change lanes. For safety, pass promptly and avoid lingering in these blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When you are one car length ahead.,c:When you are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.
note: After passing, you should not move back into the right lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have created a safe following distance and reduces the risk of cutting off the other driver or causing a rear-end collision.

question: If you must park in an unusual area, what should you ensure about your vehicle?
options: a:Make sure the vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction,b:Park five feet from the curb,c:Park with your reverse lights on,d:Place your car in neutral and turn off the engine
note: If you must park in an unusual or unexpected location, your top priority is to make sure other drivers can see your vehicle in time to react safely. Park where your vehicle is clearly visible from all directions and does not block traffic. Use hazard lights if appropriate so approaching drivers are warned of your parked vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The larger vehicle.,b:The driver on the right.,c:The one who signals first.,d:The driver on the left.
note: At an open or uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals controlling the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Signal and assume freeway traffic will stop for you.,b:Enter slowly and force traffic to adjust.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for an opening.,d:Signal, accelerate to match freeway speed, and yield to traffic already on the freeway.
note: When entering a freeway, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, signal your intention to merge, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway. Do not stop at the end of the ramp unless absolutely necessary; instead, adjust your speed and merge when it is safe.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while you're driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Rapidly pump the brake pedal,b:Slam on the brakes immediately,c:Take your foot off the accelerator and allow the vehicle to slow,d:Turn sharply toward the shoulder
note: If a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, stay straight, and take your foot off the accelerator so the vehicle can slow down gradually. Braking hard or turning sharply can cause you to lose control, especially at higher speeds.

question: What should be your first reaction to reduced visibility while driving?
options: a:Turn on windshield wipers.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Increase your following distance only.,d:Reduce your speed.
note: When visibility drops, your first reaction should be to ease off the accelerator and reduce speed so you have more time to see and react to hazards. You should also turn on your headlights and increase following distance, but slowing down is the most immediate safety step.

question: If you are on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, what should you do?
options: a:Drive toward the nearest edge or curb and stop.,b:Speed up and take the nearest exit.,c:Turn on your flashers and continue driving.
note: On a one‑way street, when an emergency vehicle with lights or siren approaches, move safely and promptly to the nearest edge or curb—right or left—and stop until it has passed. Stopping clears a path and prevents sudden conflicts as the emergency vehicle comes through.

question: On a two-lane highway, what must you do when you approach a stopped school bus with flashing red lights?
options: a:You must stop and remain stopped until the bus driver waves you through.,b:You may pass at a reduced speed if no children are visible.,c:You must stop and may not pass until the bus turns off its flashing red lights and resumes driving.
note: On a two‑lane road, traffic in both directions must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights. You must remain stopped and may not pass until the red lights stop flashing and the bus starts moving or the driver signals that you may proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what should you do to ensure safety?
options: a:Rely solely on the rearview mirror.,b:Change lanes without signaling if clear.,c:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move and check mirrors.,d:Rely only on the left side mirror.
note: Before changing lanes, always signal, check your mirrors, and then look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot. Never rely only on mirrors; the shoulder check helps you see vehicles that are hidden from your mirror view.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When traveling in a travel lane, you should:
options: a:Park briefly to drop off passengers.,b:Stop in the lane to check an address.,c:Keep moving until you can safely pull off the roadway.,d:Make a U-turn if you miss an exit.
note: You must not stop in a travel lane except in emergencies or when traffic is stopped. If you miss an exit or turn, keep driving until you reach a safe place off the roadway to pull over or turn around.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a roundabout, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, yield to traffic and pedestrians in the circle, and enter to the right.,b:Speed up to enter before other vehicles.,c:Enter to the left and drive clockwise.,d:Stop and wait for a green light.
note: At roundabouts in the U.S., you slow down, yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and to traffic already in the circle, then enter to the right and travel counterclockwise. Do not speed up to beat other vehicles, enter to the left, or wait for a traffic light unless one is present and controlling entry.

question: Anything that requires you to do which of the following could cause a crash?
options: a:Take your eyes off the road.,b:Take your hands off the wheel.,c:Take your attention away from driving.,d:Any of the above.
note: Any distraction that takes your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off driving can lead to a crash. Visual, manual, and cognitive distractions all reduce your ability to react to hazards in time.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, which action might they legally take?
options: a:Cut through all lanes without regard for traffic.,b:Always wait on the sidewalk.,c:Use the left lane when preparing to or making the left turn.,d:Only turn left from the right edge of the road.
note: Bicyclists generally have the same rights and duties as drivers of vehicles. When making a left turn, a bicyclist may legally move into and use the appropriate left-turn lane or left portion of the lane, after yielding as required and signaling, just like a motor vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should a driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp behave?
options: a:Assume they have the right-of-way and enter regardless of others.,b:Force their way into traffic.,c:Yield to drivers already on the interstate and merge when safe.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for traffic to clear completely in all lanes.
note: Traffic already on the interstate has the right-of-way. Use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic, signal, and merge only when there is a safe gap. Never force your way in or assume others must move for you.

question: What must you do when facing a green arrow signal?
options: a:Proceed immediately without yielding.,b:Turn only if no vehicles are behind you.,c:Yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection, then proceed in the direction of the arrow.,d:Wait four seconds before moving.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow, but you must still yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians already in the intersection or still clearing it. Once the intersection is clear, you may proceed with your turn.

question: If you have a sudden tire blowout, how should you use the brakes?
options: a:Use the brakes lightly after slowing down and regaining control.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly.,c:Apply full force to the brakes.,d:Do not use the brakes at all, even after you have slowed.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly and ease your foot off the accelerator so the vehicle slows gradually. Once the vehicle is under control and your speed has dropped, brake gently and lightly as needed to pull off the road safely. Hard or sudden braking can cause loss of control, especially with a blown tire.

question: When driving on wet pavement you should remember:
options: a:Roads are especially slippery right after rain begins.,b:Hydroplaning can occur at high speeds.,c:Give yourself extra space when stopping.,d:All of the above.
note: On wet pavement, roads are especially slippery just after the rain begins because oil and residue mix with water. At higher speeds your tires can ride on top of the water (hydroplaning), causing loss of traction. Always increase your following distance and brake earlier and more gently on wet roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before turning left you should:
options: a:Accelerate slightly to make the turn faster.,b:Sound your horn to warn others.,c:Swing to the right of your lane.,d:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
note: Before turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians that are close enough to be a hazard. Wait until there is a safe gap in oncoming traffic and the crosswalk is clear, then turn into the correct lane without swinging wide.

question: Which definition best matches distracted driving?
options: a:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.,b:Driving while tired only.,c:Anything that takes your attention away from driving, including your eyes, hands, or mind.,d:Only using a cellphone while driving.
note: Distracted driving is any activity that takes your attention away from driving. This includes things that take your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off driving, such as texting, eating, adjusting controls, or daydreaming.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway you should:
options: a:Drive in the truck's blind spot to stay out of traffic.,b:Always pass on the right.,c:Follow farther behind than you would a passenger vehicle.,d:Follow closer to reduce wind effects.
note: Large trucks need more distance to stop and have bigger blind spots than passenger cars. When following a truck, stay farther back than you would behind a car so you can see the road ahead and have enough time to react if the truck slows or stops suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Can drivers pass on a two-lane road when there is a single solid yellow line on their side of the centerline?
options: a:False,b:True
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means passing is not allowed because it is unsafe to move into the oncoming lane. You may only pass when the broken yellow line is on your side and the way is clear.

question: At a red light that displays a green arrow in your direction, you may proceed if:
options: a:You first come to a complete stop.,b:You wait for the circular green light.,c:You yield only to oncoming vehicles.,d:You are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected turn in that direction. You may proceed if you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear, but you must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and any vehicles already in the intersection.

question: If oncoming headlights blind you at night, what is the correct action?
options: a:Look toward the right edge of the roadway until the vehicle passes.,b:Switch to high beams to see better.,c:Look directly at the lights to get used to them.,d:Close your eyes briefly.
note: Bright oncoming headlights can temporarily blind you. To reduce glare and stay in your lane, look toward the right edge of the roadway and use it as a guide until the vehicle passes. Do not look directly at the lights or close your eyes.

question: How should you regard railroad crossings?
options: a:Safe places to park.,b:Safe to cross most of the time.,c:Dangerous; always check carefully.,d:Only dangerous at night.
note: Railroad crossings are always potentially dangerous because trains cannot stop quickly and always have the right of way. Slow down, look and listen for trains, obey all signals and gates, and never cross until you are sure it is safe and there is room to clear the tracks completely.

question: If your vehicle starts to lose traction due to water on the road (hydroplaning), what should you do?
options: a:Drive at a constant higher speed to regain traction.,b:Slow down gradually and avoid applying the brakes.,c:Apply the brakes firmly to stop immediately.
note: When your vehicle hydroplanes, the tires are riding on a thin layer of water and have little or no contact with the road. You should ease off the accelerator, keep the steering wheel straight, and slow down gradually. Avoid hard braking or sudden steering, because these can cause a complete loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or false: At a four-way stop you must yield to motorists who arrived before you.
options: a:Only if they signal.,b:Only if they are on the right.,c:False.,d:True.
note: At a four‑way stop, drivers must yield to vehicles that arrived first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right. Always proceed in the order of arrival and only when it is safe.

question: How serious is drinking alcohol and driving?
options: a:A serious traffic safety problem.,b:A minor traffic safety problem.,c:Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
note: Drinking and driving is a major cause of crashes, injuries, and deaths. Even small amounts of alcohol slow your reaction time, reduce coordination, and impair judgment. Because any impairment can make driving unsafe, alcohol and driving together are always a serious traffic safety problem.

question: True or False: Drivers should avoid driving beside large vehicles for extended periods and be cautious when passing them.
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: Large trucks and buses have large blind spots along both sides, directly behind, and sometimes directly in front of the vehicle. If you drive next to them for a long time, the driver may not see you, and a lane change or wind gust could push you into danger. It is safer to pass promptly when it is legal and safe, or drop back so you are clearly visible.

question: When you see a school crossing sign you should:
options: a:Always come to a complete stop even if no children are present.,b:Watch for children and be prepared to stop.,c:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,d:Sound your horn to clear children from the road.
note: A school crossing sign warns that children may be crossing the road. You should slow down, watch carefully for children on or near the roadway, and be prepared to stop if they are in or approaching the crosswalk. You are not required to stop if the crossing is clear, but you must be ready to do so.

question: What should you do when encountering a flashing yellow traffic light?
options: a:Yield to all traffic before crossing.,b:Stop,c:Slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down, be prepared to yield if needed, and proceed through the intersection with extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a stop is required but there is no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: a:Only if you can see at least 200 feet in both directions.,b:At the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic without entering it.,c:You are not required to stop.
note: When there is a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk, you must stop before entering the intersection at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic, without actually entering the cross street.

question: An inattentive driver is one who:
options: a:Maintains eye contact with passengers constantly.,b:Daydreams or stares off the roadway while driving.,c:Only watches the vehicle directly ahead.,d:Uses mirrors regularly.
note: An inattentive driver is mentally or visually distracted from the driving task, such as daydreaming or staring away from the roadway, which greatly increases the risk of missing hazards and causing a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:Slow speeds.,b:Driving in the rain with headlights on.,c:Night driving.,d:High speeds.
note: High speeds make it take much longer to stop and greatly increase crash severity because the force of impact rises rapidly as speed increases.

question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic light mean?
options: a:You may not proceed in the arrow's direction until it turns green,b:You may turn after yielding to oncoming traffic,c:You may turn after stopping completely,d:You may proceed with caution
note: A steady red arrow means you must stop and may not go in the direction of the arrow until a green arrow or green light allows movement in that direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic queues behind you on a two-lane road, what must you do?
options: a:Stop in the lane until traffic clears,b:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass,c:Decrease your speed further,d:Not allow other cars to pass you
note: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is building up behind you on a two‑lane road, you are impeding the normal flow of traffic. When it is safe, you should pull off to the right side of the road or into a turnout area and allow the vehicles behind you to pass. This keeps traffic moving smoothly and reduces the risk of unsafe passing maneuvers by frustrated drivers.

question: When passing a bicyclist you should:
options: a:Slow down and give the cyclist as much space as possible.,b:Drive into the bicycle lane until you can pass.,c:Honk to alert the bicyclist to move over.,d:Pass very quickly and close to the cyclist.
note: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and give them as much space as possible, following your state’s minimum passing distance (often at least 3 feet, and more at higher speeds). Treat a bicycle like any other vehicle in the lane: change lanes or move well over when safe, and never pass closely or at high speed because a small wobble or road hazard could cause a serious crash.

question: Which statement about vehicle blind spots is correct?
options: a:You can check blind spots using the inside rearview mirror.,b:Blind spots are not a safety concern.,c:Blind spots disappear if you have only one outside mirror.,d:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger cars.
note: All vehicles have blind spots—areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks and buses have much larger blind spots on all sides than passenger cars, especially directly behind and along the sides near the cab. You should avoid lingering in these areas and pass large trucks quickly and safely so the driver can see you.

question: At about what speed can cars begin to hydroplane on standing water?
options: a:40 miles per hour,b:45 miles per hour,c:35 miles per hour
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride up on a layer of water and lose contact with the road. This can begin at speeds as low as about 35 mph on standing water, especially if your tires are worn or the water is deep. To reduce the risk, slow down in wet conditions, avoid sudden steering or braking, and make sure your tires are in good condition.

question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or carrying a white cane, you must:
options: a:Flash your headlights to alert them.,b:Honk to warn them to wait.,c:Continue driving; pedestrians must yield.,d:Yield the right-of-way to the pedestrian.
note: A pedestrian using a white cane or a guide dog is visually impaired and has special legal protection. You must always yield the right‑of‑way, stop well before the crosswalk, and allow them to cross safely. Do not honk or try to wave them on; remain stopped until they are safely out of your path.

question: Faced with an oncoming car to the left and a bicyclist to the right, what is safest?
options: a:Split the difference and pass between them.,b:Let the oncoming car pass,c:Attempt to pass both at once quickly.,d:Pull onto the shoulder between the two hazards.
note: When you face hazards on both sides, you should not try to squeeze between them. Instead, deal with one hazard at a time. In this case, slow down and let the oncoming car pass first, then move over and pass the bicyclist with plenty of space when it is safe.

question: Are you required to obey school crossing guards?
options: a:At all times.,b:Only during school hours.,c:Only when children are present.
note: School crossing guards have legal authority to direct traffic. You must obey their instructions whenever they are on duty and directing traffic, regardless of the time of day or whether you see children in the crosswalk.

question: Should motorists keep a safe operating distance when near cyclists?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: Cyclists are vulnerable road users, so you must give them extra space and time. Maintain a safe following distance—at least three to four seconds—and allow plenty of room when passing so you have time to react if they need to swerve or stop.

question: Which types of drugs can affect your driving ability?
options: a:Only illegal drugs.,b:Over-the-counter,c:Only prescriptions.,d:Illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter drugs can all affect driving.
note: Any drug that affects your mind or body can impair driving, including illegal drugs, prescription medications, and over‑the‑counter medicines. Always read labels and follow medical advice, and never drive if a drug makes you drowsy, dizzy, or less alert.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Speeding is never fatal.,b:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,c:Speeding is not dangerous if you are skilled.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because it may cause other drivers to brake suddenly or make risky passing maneuvers. Safe driving means adjusting your speed to match traffic and road conditions, without exceeding the speed limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:Only if the pedestrian waves to you.,b:Only if the pedestrian is not distracted.,c:At all times.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians who are in a marked or unmarked crosswalk. You must slow or stop as needed to let pedestrians cross safely, regardless of whether they make eye contact, signal, or appear distracted.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You have the right-of-way at all railroad crossings,b:You need not stop for a crossing without gates,c:You may pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is safe,d:You must stop when directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign at a crossing
note: At railroad crossings, trains always have the right-of-way. You must stop when a flagger, stop sign, or other traffic control device at the crossing requires it, and you must never drive onto the tracks unless you can fully clear them.

question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe,b:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is prohibited,c:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is prohibited,d:You may cross to pass if no cars are coming
note: A double solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means no passing from either side. You must stay in your lane and may only cross when making a permitted turn or when specifically allowed by law.

question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of the road indicate about passing?
options: a:Passing allowed only during daylight.,b:Passing is allowed from both directions.,c:Only the right lane may pass.,d:Passing is not allowed from either direction, except for permitted turns where allowed by law.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic in opposite directions and no passing from either direction. In most situations you may not cross these lines to pass another vehicle; you may only cross when making a lawful left turn or when specifically allowed by local law.

question: When emergency vehicles are using sirens and flashing lights, what must drivers do?
options: a:Follow closely behind them,b:Ignore them and continue driving,c:Pull into the intersection and wait,d:Yield the right-of-way to them
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using a siren and flashing lights, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling to the right side of the road and stopping, when safe. Remain stopped until the vehicle has passed and always follow any directions given by emergency personnel.

question: Where is it illegal to park?
options: a:On a hill,b:In a parking lot,c:In front of your driveway,d:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane
note: It is illegal and unsafe to park where you block traffic or other road users, such as on a crosswalk, in a marked bicycle lane, or in front of a driveway. Parking on a hill or in a parking lot is allowed as long as there are no signs or markings prohibiting it and your vehicle is properly secured.

question: At dawn, dusk, or in rain or snow when visibility is reduced, what should you do to help others see you?
options: a:Flash your high beams,b:Use only your parking lights,c:Increase your instrument panel brightness,d:Turn on your headlights
note: Use your headlights, specifically low beams, whenever visibility is reduced by rain, snow, fog, or at dawn and dusk. This makes your vehicle easier for others to see without creating glare, which can happen if you use high beams in poor conditions.

question: What are "No zones" around large trucks?
options: a:Areas where you can squeeze around while it turns.,b:Areas where smaller cars disappear into the truck's blind spots.,c:Safe spaces to travel close behind the truck.,d:Designated passenger loading zones.
note: "No zones" are the large blind spots around trucks and other big vehicles where your car may completely disappear from the truck driver’s view. Avoid driving for long periods directly beside, very close in front of, or close behind a large truck so the driver can see you and react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parked uphill on a street with a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels sharply toward the curb,b:Turn the wheels slightly to the right,c:Turn the wheels sharply away from the curb,d:Point the wheels straight ahead
note: When you park facing uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will move toward and rest against the curb, helping prevent the car from rolling into traffic.

question: How should you respond to a steady yellow arrow traffic signal?
options: a:Honk to alert other drivers,b:Proceed immediately without yielding,c:Merge into any lane shown by the arrow,d:Stop if you can do so safely; a red arrow is coming
note: A steady yellow arrow means the protected turn phase is ending and a red arrow is about to appear. You should stop if you can do so safely. If you are too close to the intersection to stop safely, proceed with caution and be prepared for the light to change.

question: If another car appears likely to hit you, what should you do first?
options: a:Sound your horn to warn the other driver.,b:Wave your arms out the window.,c:Use emergency lights only.
note: If another car may hit you, your first action should be to try to prevent the collision by warning the other driver. Sounding your horn is the quickest way to alert them that they are about to collide with you. Waving your arms or relying only on emergency flashers is slower and less effective in an immediate emergency.

question: Which item is a common contributing factor to crashes?
options: a:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,b:Exceeding speed limits or driving too fast for conditions.,c:Scanning the environment and staying focused on driving.
note: Speeding or driving too fast for road, traffic, or weather conditions is one of the most common causes of crashes. Higher speed reduces your time to react and increases stopping distance and crash severity. In contrast, getting adequate rest and scanning the road ahead are safe driving habits that help prevent collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at an intersection with a flashing red light. What must you do?
options: a:Wait for a green light to appear.,b:Stop at the intersection and then proceed when the way is clear.,c:Turn right only.,d:Slow and drive through the intersection without stopping.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield as necessary, and then proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: If the roadway ahead is flooded, what should you do?
options: a:Try to drive through at low speed.,b:Slam on the brakes to avoid water.,c:Turn around and find another route; do not drive through flooded areas.,d:Drive only in the center of the roadway.
note: You should never drive through flooded roadways. Water can be deeper or moving faster than it appears, can hide holes or debris, and even a small depth can sweep a vehicle away or stall it. The safest action is to turn around and find another route.

question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of the road indicate?
options: a:Passing is permitted from either direction when safe.,b:A construction zone ahead.,c:Passing is prohibited for both directions.,d:Bike lane separation.
note: A broken yellow line in the center separates traffic moving in opposite directions and indicates that passing is allowed from either direction when it can be done safely. You must still check for oncoming traffic, ensure enough space to pass, and obey any additional signs or markings.

question: When driving in traffic, what is the safest practice regarding speed?
options: a:Drive faster than the flow of traffic,b:Drive with the flow of traffic within the posted speed limit,c:Fluctuate your speed frequently to stay alert,d:Drive slower than the flow of traffic
note: In traffic, you should generally move with the flow of traffic while staying at or below the posted speed limit. Large speed differences between you and surrounding vehicles increase the risk of rear-end and side-swipe collisions. Driving much faster or much slower than other traffic is unsafe; instead, match the general flow as long as it is within legal and safe limits.

question: What is the safest way for small children to ride in a vehicle?
options: a:Held by a strong adult.,b:Standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.,c:Secured in an appropriate child safety seat or seat belt for their size.
note: Small children must always be properly restrained in a child safety seat or seat belt that is appropriate for their age, height, and weight. In a crash, an adult cannot safely hold a child, and standing or moving around in the vehicle is extremely dangerous. Properly installed child restraints greatly reduce the risk of serious injury.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are typically what color?
options: a:Yellow.,b:Orange.,c:White.,d:Green.
note: Regulatory signs tell you about traffic laws and regulations you must obey, such as speed limits, lane use, and parking restrictions. In the U.S., these signs are typically white rectangles or squares with black, red, or green lettering or symbols. Yellow signs are usually warning signs, not regulatory.

question: When you approach a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog who is crossing, you must:
options: a:Carefully drive around them.,b:Sound your horn and proceed slowly.,c:Stop until the pedestrian is safely out of your path.
note: When a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog is crossing or preparing to cross, you must stop and remain stopped until the person has completely crossed and is safely out of your path. Blind pedestrians have the right-of-way, and sudden noises like horns can startle them or their guide dogs.

question: On a four-lane highway, if you approach a stopped school bus on the opposite side with red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:You may continue driving; you are not required to stop when approaching from the opposite side.,b:Stop regardless of how many lanes there are.,c:Pass slowly while watching for children.
note: On a divided or multi-lane highway (typically four or more lanes) where there is a physical median or barrier, drivers traveling in the opposite direction of a stopped school bus with flashing red lights are usually not required to stop. However, they must slow down, use extreme caution, and be prepared for children who may be near the roadway. Always check your state’s specific rules, as some states require all traffic to stop on undivided roads regardless of lane count.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway you should be traveling:
options: a:Much slower than freeway traffic.,b:At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.,c:At the speed recommended by signage only.,d:At the posted speed limit only.
note: When using a freeway on‑ramp, use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic already on the freeway, as long as you do not exceed the speed limit. Entering too slowly forces other drivers to brake or swerve, while entering too fast can be unsafe and illegal.

question: In a vehicle with airbags, where is the safest place for children age 12 and under to ride?
options: a:In the back seat.,b:In the bed of a pickup truck.,c:In the front passenger seat.
note: Children age 12 and under are safest in the back seat, properly secured in the correct child safety seat or seat belt for their size. Front airbags are designed for adults and can seriously injure small children in a crash, so they should not ride in the front passenger seat when a back seat is available.

question: When approaching railroad tracks, how should you prepare?
options: a:Speed up to clear the crossing quickly.,b:Drive around lowered gates if you don't see a train.,c:Look and listen for trains, slow down, and be prepared to stop if necessary.
note: Always approach railroad crossings with caution. Slow down, look both ways, and listen for trains, even if signals are not flashing. Be prepared to stop if a train is approaching or if warning devices are activated, and never try to beat a train through the crossing.

question: When approaching the scene of an accident, what is the correct behavior?
options: a:Drive to the scene to offer eyewitness accounts.,b:Stop and gather around to watch.,c:Keep your attention on driving and keep moving unless you are involved or help is needed.
note: When you come upon a crash scene, keep your attention on the road and continue driving unless you are directly involved or emergency help is clearly needed and you can safely assist. Unnecessary stopping or slowing to look creates additional hazards and can cause more collisions.

question: Which of the following is true about passing a motorcycle?
options: a:You do not need to be fully in the adjacent lane to pass.,b:You may pass a motorcycle without changing lanes.,c:The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.,d:Motorcycles must share lane markings so you can pass closely.
note: Motorcycles occupy a full lane; drivers must move completely into the left lane when passing a motorcycle from the left.

question: A diamond-shaped roadway sign indicates what type of message?
options: a:A regulatory command you must follow.,b:Warning about a road hazard or special condition ahead.,c:A school crossing only.,d:An interstate route marker.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are used for warnings. They alert you to upcoming hazards or special conditions such as curves, merging traffic, or pedestrian crossings so you can adjust speed and be prepared.

question: If your wheels drop off the roadway or pavement edge, what should you do?
options: a:Turn back onto the roadway immediately and sharply.,b:Slow down, keep control, and return to the road gradually when it is safe.,c:Stop and call for help.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, stay calm, ease off the gas, and keep steering straight. After you have slowed and checked for traffic, gently steer back onto the roadway when there is a safe gap. Do not jerk the wheel or turn sharply, as this can cause you to lose control or swerve into another lane.

question: What common mistake do drivers make when backing up?
options: a:Signaling too early,b:Relying solely on rearview mirrors,c:Failing to turn their head and look both ways out the rear window,d:Backing up slowly
note: When backing up, you must turn your head and look through the rear window in the direction of travel. Relying only on mirrors can hide children, pedestrians, or objects in blind spots, increasing the risk of a collision.

question: True or false: If traffic is moving across a railroad track in a stream, it is safe to stop on the track briefly.
options: a:True.,b:Only if no train is visible.,c:False.,d:Only in an emergency.
note: Never stop on railroad tracks, even briefly. Only enter a crossing if there is enough space on the far side for your entire vehicle to clear the tracks. Trains cannot stop quickly, and being stopped on the tracks is extremely dangerous and illegal.

question: Why are roads especially slippery just after rain begins, and what should you do?
options: a:Increase your speed to avoid puddles.,b:Test tire traction while going uphill.,c:Decrease how far ahead you look.,d:Roads are slippery and you should slow down and avoid fast turns or stops.
note: When rain first begins, oil and residue on the road mix with water and make the surface very slippery. You should slow down, increase following distance, and avoid fast turns or sudden stops so your tires can maintain traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the maximum speed limit in a rural area unless a higher limit is allowed by federal law?
options: a:60 mph,b:55 mph,c:40 mph,d:50 mph
note: On most U.S. DMV exams, the general maximum speed limit in rural areas (where not otherwise posted) is 55 mph, unless a higher limit is specifically posted or allowed by law. Always follow the posted speed limit; if no sign is present, use the general statutory limit for that type of road and area.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are motorists required to yield to pedestrians who cross against a traffic signal?
options: a:False — drivers must still do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, even one crossing against the signal.,b:True — pedestrians walking against a signal have no claim to right-of-way.,c:Only on highways.,d:Only at marked crosswalks.
note: Drivers must do everything reasonably possible to avoid hitting pedestrians, even when the pedestrian is crossing against the signal and does not have the legal right-of-way. You should slow or stop if needed to prevent a collision, while still recognizing that a pedestrian walking against a signal is not lawfully entitled to the right-of-way.

question: Combining drugs with alcohol:
options: a:Increases the risk of causing a crash.,b:Lessens alcohol's effects.,c:Is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.,d:Only impacts long trips.
note: Mixing alcohol with any drugs—prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal—greatly increases impairment. The combined effects can be stronger and less predictable than either substance alone, which significantly raises the risk of causing a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road, what should you do?
options: a:Pass without checking mirrors if the road looks clear.,b:Sound your horn continuously while passing.,c:Judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles carefully.,d:Flash your headlights as a signal to pass.
note: Before passing on a two-lane road, you must carefully judge the speed and distance of oncoming traffic and be sure you have enough clear space to complete the pass safely. Only move into the opposing lane when you are certain you can pass and return to your lane without interfering with oncoming vehicles.

question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:
options: a:Flashing red signals and gates are operating.,b:Directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign.,c:All of the above.,d:The crossing is controlled by a stop sign.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing whenever flashing red lights are operating, gates are down or coming down, a stop sign is posted, or a flagger or other traffic control device directs you to stop. Always obey these warnings and do not proceed until you are sure no train is approaching and it is clearly safe to cross.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive at a speed greater than which of the following?
options: a:The posted maximum speed only.,b:A speed that is safe for the conditions only.,c:A speed that is faster than is reasonable and prudent for existing conditions.
note: You must never drive faster than is reasonable and prudent for current conditions, even if that speed is below the posted limit. The basic speed law requires you to adjust your speed for rain, fog, traffic, curves, and visibility so you can stop safely within the distance you can see ahead.

question: If your tire blows out while driving, what is the correct initial reaction?
options: a:Slam on the brakes immediately,b:Speed up to reach a safe area,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly and gradually slow to a stop,d:Jump out of the car
note: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle going straight, and gently ease off the accelerator. Once you have the car under control and your speed has dropped, move to the side of the road and stop in a safe place. Slamming on the brakes can cause loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when should you return to your original lane?
options: a:As soon as you clear the front bumper of the vehicle.,b:When you are 50 feet ahead of the vehicle.,c:When you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space and do not cut off the other driver.

question: How should you behave when another vehicle is passing you?
options: a:Brake hard to prevent them from passing.,b:Honk continuously to warn them off.,c:Speed up to keep your position.,d:Maintain a steady speed and allow them to pass.
note: When another vehicle is passing you, stay in your lane, maintain a steady speed, and, if necessary, slightly reduce speed to help them pass safely. Never speed up or brake suddenly while you are being passed.

question: Is it ever acceptable to drive around or under a moving railroad crossing gate?
options: a:If you first look carefully in both directions.,b:Never; do not drive around or under a lowering or lowered gate.,c:If an approaching train is not too close.
note: You must never drive around, under, or through a railroad crossing gate that is lowering, lowered, or rising. Flashing lights and gates mean a train is approaching or nearby, and trains cannot stop quickly. Always wait until the lights stop flashing and the gates are fully raised before crossing.

question: Alcohol is classified as which type of substance?
options: a:A stimulant.,b:A hallucinogen.,c:A depressant.,d:An antihistamine.
note: Alcohol is classified as a depressant. It slows activity in the central nervous system, which reduces reaction time, coordination, and judgment. Even small amounts can affect your ability to drive safely.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Drive faster than the train to beat it across,b:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby,c:Ignore it if you do not see tracks,d:Drive around any lowered gates
note: A railroad crossing warning sign means you are approaching tracks and must be ready to slow or stop. Look and listen for trains, and never try to beat a train or drive around lowered gates.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:School zones.,b:No passing zones.,c:Railroad crossings.
note: A crossbuck is the white X-shaped sign that marks a railroad crossing. It tells you to yield to trains, look and listen carefully, and obey any flashing lights or gates.

question: Is it wise to continually improve your driving and observation skills?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Driving always involves changing conditions and risks, so it is wise to keep improving your observation, judgment, and vehicle-handling skills. Better skills help you spot hazards early and avoid collisions.

question: Is parking in a handicap access aisle beside a handicap stall permitted?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Parking in the striped handicap access aisle is not allowed. These areas provide extra space for wheelchair users and lifts to safely enter and exit vehicles parked in designated disabled spaces.

question: If you are about to be struck from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly,b:Be ready to apply the brakes if necessary,c:Brace against the seat back and put your head against the head restraint,d:Release your seat belt
note: If you are about to be hit from the rear, keep your seat belt fastened, hold the steering wheel firmly, and press your head and back against the seat and head restraint. This helps control the vehicle and reduces the risk of whiplash or being thrown forward.

question: Which ability is affected first by alcohol?
options: a:Judgment.,b:Vision.,c:Balance.,d:Hearing.
note: Alcohol first affects judgment and decision‑making, even when you may feel normal. This reduced judgment makes you more likely to take risks, misjudge distances, and react poorly, long before you notice major changes in vision, balance, or hearing.

question: What does the acronym BAC stand for?
options: a:Blood alcohol consent,b:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC),c:Body alcohol content,d:Base alcohol content
note: BAC stands for blood alcohol concentration. It is a measurement of how much alcohol is in a person’s bloodstream and is used to determine legal impairment for driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you stop at an intersection because of a signal?
options: a:When you see a flashing red light.,b:When you see a steady yellow light.,c:When you see a yellow arrow.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign, and then proceed only when it is safe. A steady yellow warns that the light is about to turn red, and a yellow arrow warns that the protected turn is ending; you are not always required to stop immediately for those.

question: When exiting the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill, what should you do?
options: a:Maintain freeway speed until halfway down the ramp.,b:Reduce speed to a safe level before entering the curve.,c:Brake sharply while in the curve.,d:Shift to neutral before the curve.
note: On a downhill, curving exit ramp, you should slow to a safe speed before you enter the curve. Braking hard while in the curve can cause skidding or loss of control, especially on a downgrade.

question: Why should you leave extra space in front of a large truck?
options: a:So other drivers can merge onto the freeway.,b:So other drivers have room to slow down in front of the truck.,c:Because trucks take longer to stop and need extra room to stop safely.
note: Large trucks are heavier and need a much longer distance to stop than passenger cars. Leaving extra space in front of a truck gives the truck driver the room needed to brake safely if traffic slows or stops suddenly, reducing the risk of a rear‑end collision.

question: What is true about tailgating (following too closely)?
options: a:It cannot lead to a traffic citation.,b:It reduces collisions by preventing being cut off.,c:Is encouraged on busy roads.,d:It can anger other drivers and may result in legal consequences.
note: Tailgating increases the chance of collisions and contributes to aggressive driving; it can also lead to citations.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Leave a note with your name and address securely attached to the parked vehicle.,b:Wait indefinitely for the owner to return.,c:Call your insurance only after you get home.
note: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, you must stop, leave a note with your name, address, and contact information securely on the vehicle, and follow any required reporting laws. This ensures the owner can contact you and that the collision is properly documented.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While you are crossing an intersection and an emergency vehicle with siren and lights approaches, you should:
options: a:Pull to the left and stop.,b:Continue through the intersection,c:Stop immediately in the intersection.,d:Speed up and clear the intersection quickly.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, you must yield by pulling to the right and stopping. If you are already in an intersection, continue through it first, then pull to the right and stop as soon as it is safe. Stopping in the intersection can block traffic and the emergency vehicle.

question: If your vehicle has airbags, what should you also do for maximum protection?
options: a:Rely on the airbags alone.,b:Always wear your seat belt in combination with airbags.,c:Wear the lap belt behind your back.
note: Airbags are designed to work together with seat belts, not replace them. For maximum protection, always wear your lap and shoulder belt properly even in a vehicle equipped with airbags, as seat belts help keep you in position so the airbag can protect you effectively.

question: Why is driving at night generally more difficult than driving during the day?
options: a:Cars overheat more quickly at night.,b:It is more likely to rain at night.,c:Visibility is reduced in the dark.
note: Driving at night is harder because you cannot see as far or as clearly as in daylight. Headlights limit your field of vision, and hazards, pedestrians, and road signs are harder to detect. Always use proper headlights and drive slowly enough that you can stop within the distance you can see ahead.

question: Which road marking or device is commonly used on some highways to indicate which lanes are for turning?
options: a:White lines on the side of the road.,b:Arrows painted on the roadway and lane-use markings.,c:Flashing red lights on the shoulder.
note: On many roads, arrows and lane-use markings are painted directly on the pavement to show which lanes are for turning or going straight. These markings help drivers get into the correct lane before an intersection and reduce last‑second lane changes.

question: True or False: Ramps and bridges tend to freeze before the main road surface.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only during heavy snow,d:Only in shaded areas
note: Bridges and ramps freeze first because they are exposed to cold air above and below, unlike regular road surfaces that are insulated by the ground. Even when the main roadway looks just wet, bridges and ramps can be icy, so you should slow down and use extra caution when temperatures are near freezing.

question: At a school crossing sign, how should you behave?
options: a:Always stop regardless of circumstances.,b:Sound your horn to warn children.,c:Drive faster to clear the area quickly.,d:Watch closely for children and be ready to stop.
note: At a school crossing, you must slow down, watch carefully for children, and be prepared to stop at any time. Children may behave unpredictably, so you should be extra alert, obey any crossing guard, and always yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part seat belt system, you should:
options: a:Use only the lap belt.,b:Use both the lap and shoulder belts.,c:Use only the shoulder belt.,d:Use neither if the airbags are present.
note: In a two‑part seat belt system, the lap belt and shoulder belt are designed to work together. The lap belt keeps your lower body in place, and the shoulder belt helps protect your head and chest in a crash. Using both greatly reduces the risk of serious injury compared with using only one part or none.

question: If you observe other drivers acting angrily, what should you do?
options: a:Distance yourself from the situation and get away safely,b:Don’t make eye contact and avoid gestures,c:React with hand gestures to show displeasure,d:Challenge them to change behavior
note: When you encounter an angry or aggressive driver, your priority is to stay safe and avoid escalating the situation. Create space between your vehicle and the aggressive driver and, when it is safe, leave the area or change routes. Avoid eye contact and do not respond with gestures or challenges, as this can provoke road rage and increase the risk of a crash.

question: If there is no marked crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane, you should:
options: a:Make sure the pedestrian sees you before proceeding rapidly.,b:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.,d:Honk to warn the pedestrian.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even if there is no marked crosswalk; stop and let them cross safely.

question: When is it appropriate to honk your horn?
options: a:To express frustration at another driver.,b:To warn others of an immediate danger,c:Every time you pass another vehicle.,d:When traveling through an intersection.
note: Your horn is a safety device used to warn others of immediate danger, such as when another driver is about to move into your lane or a pedestrian steps into your path without seeing you. It should not be used to express anger, to greet people, or routinely at intersections.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While waiting in the intersection to complete a left turn, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Flash your headlights to get other drivers to yield,b:Signal and keep your wheels straight,c:Turn wheels sharply to the right,d:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left
note: When waiting in an intersection to turn left, keep your front wheels pointed straight ahead until you actually begin the turn. If your wheels are turned left and you are hit from behind, your vehicle can be pushed into oncoming traffic. Keeping the wheels straight reduces this risk and allows you to stay in your lane if struck.

question: A pentagon-shaped traffic sign is used to indicate:
options: a:A regulatory command.,b:A general warning of hazards.,c:A stop requirement.,d:A school zone or school crossing.
note: Pentagon-shaped signs are used for school zones and school crossings. When you see this five-sided sign, be prepared to slow down, watch for children, and obey any reduced speed limits or crossing guard instructions in the area.

question: What information do blue road signs provide?
options: a:Mileage and distance to locations.,b:Motorist services such as food,c:Construction and maintenance warnings.
note: Blue road signs are service signs. They point to facilities and services for drivers, such as gas stations, restaurants, lodging, rest areas, hospitals, and telephones so you can find help and amenities while traveling.

question: What color are guide (destination) signs that show directions and mileage?
options: a:Green,b:Red,c:Blue,d:Yellow
note: Guide or destination signs that show directions and mileage are green. These signs help you navigate by giving route information, directions to cities or exits, and distances to upcoming destinations.

question: Driving significantly slower than surrounding traffic is:
