options: a:Only acceptable in bad weather.,b:Always safer than driving at the flow of traffic.,c:Recommended when you are unsure of the limit.,d:Often a hazard because others may try risky passes.
note: Driving much slower than surrounding traffic can be dangerous because it disrupts the normal flow and may cause other drivers to brake suddenly or make risky passing maneuvers. When conditions allow, you should travel near the flow of traffic while staying at or below the posted speed limit.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you should:
options: a:Increase speed to clear the intersection.,b:Stop before entering the intersection.,c:Wait for a green light.,d:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution. Look carefully for cross traffic, pedestrians, and other hazards, and continue through the intersection only when it is safe to do so. You are not required to stop unless needed for safety.

question: When should you use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?
options: a:When weather reduces visibility so others can see you.,b:Only during heavy rainstorms.,c:To warn others of bad weather without using wipers.,d:It is not required to use headlights in rain.
note: In rain, snow, or fog, you should turn on your low-beam headlights whenever visibility is reduced so that you can see and be seen more easily. In many states, the law requires headlights to be on whenever your windshield wipers are in continuous use.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you face a green traffic light but pedestrians are in the intersection, you must:
options: a:Proceed because you have the green light.,b:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,c:Signal and continue through the intersection.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection.
note: When you have a green light, you may go only if the intersection is clear. Pedestrians already in the crosswalk have the right-of-way, even against your green. You must wait until they have safely crossed before proceeding or turning.

question: What is true about driving on wet roadways?
options: a:As speed increases, tires become less effective at removing water and may hydroplane.,b:Good tires eliminate all wet-road risks.,c:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.,d:Water improves tire traction at high speeds.
note: On wet roads, as your speed increases, your tires cannot squeeze water out of the way as effectively. This can cause hydroplaning, where your tires ride on top of the water and lose contact with the road. To reduce this risk, slow down in wet conditions and make sure your tires are in good condition.

question: Which statements about steering are true?
options: a:Both of the above are incorrect.,b:Keep your thumbs inside the rim at all times.,c:Hands should be on opposite outside rim positions and use one hand only for backing or controls.,d:Always steer with one hand while driving.
note: For normal driving, place your hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel (commonly around 9-and-3 or 8-and-4) with your thumbs resting on the outside of the rim, not hooked inside. This gives you better control and reduces injury risk if the airbag deploys. Use one hand on the wheel only briefly when backing straight or when you must reach for a control, and return to a two‑handed grip as soon as possible.

question: How can you avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive and use alternatives such as taxis.,b:Just say “No thanks, I’m driving” after you start drinking.,c:Drink only beer so it is safer.,d:Wait five minutes before driving after stopping drinking.
note: The safest way to avoid an alcohol‑related crash is to decide in advance that if you drink, you will not drive. Plan a sober ride such as a taxi, rideshare, public transit, or a designated driver. Once you have started drinking, your judgment is already affected, so you cannot reliably decide later that you are “okay to drive.”

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must you yield the right-of-way to an emergency vehicle using siren and flashing lights?
options: a:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.,b:Stop immediately wherever you are.,c:Drive as close to the right edge of the road as possible and stop.,d:Proceed normally unless the emergency vehicle is directly behind you.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using a siren and flashing lights, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling as close as safely possible to the right edge of the road and stopping. Do not stop in an intersection; clear the intersection first, then pull over and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.

question: What color lines divide lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Red,d:Blue
note: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction, so yellow is the correct color for opposing traffic.

question: When parallel parking, the recommended approach is to:
options: a:Stop parallel to the vehicle ahead of the space and back into the space.,b:Signal right,c:Drive into the space forward and back up as needed.,d:Park without signaling to avoid confusing others.
note: When parallel parking, signal, pull up even with the vehicle ahead of the space, and back in, parking within 18 inches of the curb.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what three actions are important?
options: a:Signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before moving.,b:Only signal and change lanes quickly.,c:Check mirrors after you have moved into the lane.,d:Change lanes without signaling if no one seems nearby.
note: Before changing lanes, you should always: (1) signal your intention, (2) check your mirrors, and (3) check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder. Only move when the lane is clear and safe.

question: To reduce the chance of skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:
options: a:Test your tires by braking sharply while turning.,b:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.,c:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill only.,d:Speed up before entering curves and brake in the curve.
note: On slippery roads, reduce speed and slow down before curves and intersections. Braking or turning suddenly on a slick surface can cause your tires to lose traction and the vehicle to skid.

question: What should you do before starting a parked vehicle?
options: a:Adjust the side mirror and make sure the heater works.,b:Check the fuel gauge and adjust the radio volume.,c:Adjust the seat and mirrors and fasten your safety belt.,d:Check around the vehicle and then start driving without adjusting anything.
note: Before starting a parked vehicle, adjust your seat so you can reach the controls comfortably, set your mirrors for a clear view behind and to the sides, and fasten your safety belt. Doing this before moving helps you maintain control and awareness as soon as the vehicle is in motion.

question: When you see an approaching emergency vehicle using flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Move into the right lane and drive slowly.,b:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.,c:Speed up to clear the way.,d:Maintain your speed and lane until it passes.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using flashing lights and/or a siren, you are required to pull as far to the right as is safely possible and stop. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed. This gives them a clear path and reduces the chance of a collision.

question: Which statement about tires is correct?
options: a:Under-inflated tires provide a smoother ride,b:Tires must have good tread and be free of damage,c:Over-inflated tires do not skid on wet roads,d:Tires do not need regular inspection
note: Tires must have adequate tread depth and be free of cuts, bulges, or other damage to maintain traction and reduce the risk of blowouts. They should be inspected regularly for wear and proper inflation to ensure safe handling and stopping distances.

question: If you've had several beers, which action will actually reduce the effects of alcohol?
options: a:Drink several cups of coffee.,b:Wait several hours.,c:Take a cold shower.
note: Only time reduces the effects of alcohol. Your body needs time to metabolize alcohol, and nothing you do—such as drinking coffee, taking a cold shower, or exercising—will speed this up. As a rough guide, it takes about one hour for the body to process one standard drink, but this can vary by person.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit sign represent?
options: a:The maximum legal driving speed under ideal conditions.,b:Only a recommended safe speed.,c:The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket in all conditions.,d:A minimum speed requirement.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed allowed on that road in ideal conditions. You must drive slower when conditions are less than ideal, such as in rain, fog, heavy traffic, or poor visibility, so that you can stop safely and maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you never do when preparing to change lanes?
options: a:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,b:Move into another lane while inside an intersection.,c:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
note: You should not change lanes while you are in the middle of an intersection because traffic movements are more complex and other drivers may not expect a lane change there. Instead, change lanes before or after the intersection, and always signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?
options: a:It forces others to yield to you,b:It lets other road users know your intentions,c:It is illegal to turn off your signal early,d:It is unsafe to signal before a turn
note: You should signal continuously while turning so that other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians clearly understand what you are about to do. Keeping your signal on through the entire turn gives others time to react and adjust their speed or position, which reduces the chance of a collision. The law requires you to signal for a certain distance before turning and to keep signaling until the turn or lane change is completed, not because it is illegal to cancel the signal early in all circumstances, but because clear communication is essential for safety.

question: Which traffic control device corresponds to coming to a full stop, yielding to others, then proceeding when clear?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A solid green light.,c:A flashing red light.,d:A steady red arrow.
note: A flashing red light means you must stop completely, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, you must yield to any pedestrians or vehicles that have the right-of-way, and then proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe. This is different from a flashing yellow light, where you slow down and proceed with caution without stopping if the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road when meeting an oncoming vehicle, you must:
options: a:Demand the other vehicle yield to you.,b:Drive onto the shoulder at all costs.,c:Pull completely off the road and stop.,d:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.
note: On a narrow two-way road, each driver must share the available pavement so that both vehicles can pass safely. You are required to allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road. You should slow down and move as far to the right as is safe, but you are not required to drive off the road or onto the shoulder unless it is necessary and safe to avoid a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you begin reducing speed as you prepare to exit an interstate?
options: a:Only after reaching the exit ramp.,b:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.,c:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,d:As you approach the deceleration lane.
note: On an interstate, you should maintain freeway speed until you reach the deceleration lane for your exit. Once you are in the deceleration lane, you can begin slowing down to the posted advisory speed for the exit ramp. Slowing down before you enter the deceleration lane can surprise drivers behind you and disrupt the flow of traffic on the main freeway lanes.

question: True or False: Large trucks can have blind spots extending up to 200 feet behind them.
options: a:Only when heavily loaded,b:FALSE,c:TRUE,d:Only on highways
note: Large trucks and other big commercial vehicles have very large blind spots, especially directly behind them. These blind spots can extend up to about 200 feet to the rear, where the truck driver may not be able to see you in their mirrors. If you follow too closely behind a truck, the driver may not know you are there, and you will have less time to react if the truck slows or stops suddenly. Always leave extra following distance and avoid lingering in a truck’s blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians,b:Expect oncoming traffic to yield to you,c:Turn without yielding if you have a signal,d:Begin your turn as soon as the light turns green
note: When turning left, you must always yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right have the right-of-way unless they are facing a red light or stop sign. Only begin your left turn when there is a safe gap and the crosswalk is clear.

question: Sudden gusts of wind on highways can:
options: a:Cause problems for all vehicles.,b:Only affect large vehicles.,c:Only reduce visibility.,d:Only affect motorcycles.
note: Strong or sudden gusts of wind can push or destabilize any vehicle, especially at highway speeds. Large vehicles, motorcycles, and vehicles with trailers are more affected, but all drivers should be prepared to steer smoothly and reduce speed if necessary. Wind can also blow dust or debris, reducing visibility.

question: Warning signs that indicate upcoming hazards typically use which color scheme?
options: a:Black symbols on yellow.,b:Red letters on yellow.,c:White letters on blue.,d:Black symbols on white.
note: General warning signs in the United States are typically yellow with black symbols or lettering. They alert drivers to upcoming hazards such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings. Construction and maintenance warning signs use orange with black symbols.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn prohibited?
options: a:On or near any curve or hill.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a straight road with 500 feet clear view both ways.,d:At intersections with stop signs.
note: You must not make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill where you cannot see oncoming traffic from both directions. Limited visibility makes it unsafe because approaching drivers may not have time to react. Only make U-turns where they are not prohibited by signs and where you have a clear view and enough space to turn safely.

question: When is it legal to drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:If you can see clearly both directions.,b:If the warning lights are not flashing.,c:Never.
note: It is never legal to drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate. A train may be approaching faster or more quietly than you expect, or a second train may be coming. Always wait until the gates are fully raised and the warning lights and bells have stopped before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these should you never do when changing lanes?
options: a:Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.,b:Change lanes abruptly or without signaling.,c:Look over your shoulder to check the blind spot.
note: When changing lanes, you must always signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. You should never change lanes abruptly or without signaling because other drivers will not be prepared for your movement and a collision can easily occur.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While merging onto an interstate, what is the correct action?
options: a:Select a safe gap and merge into the flow of traffic at a matching speed.,b:Always stop on the ramp before entering.,c:Merge across two lanes at once to reach your destination faster.,d:Enter slowly and expect traffic to yield.
note: When merging onto an interstate, use the acceleration lane to reach a speed close to that of traffic on the highway, then select a safe gap and merge. You must yield to vehicles already on the freeway and avoid stopping on the ramp unless traffic or signals require it.

question: An orange and red triangular sign on the rear of a vehicle indicates:
options: a:A slow-moving vehicle.,b:Shoulder work ahead.,c:The vehicle has the right-of-way.,d:The vehicle is oversized.
note: An orange and red triangular emblem on the rear of a vehicle is a slow-moving vehicle sign. It warns that the vehicle usually travels 25 mph or less, such as farm equipment or certain maintenance vehicles, so you should be prepared to slow down and pass only when safe and legal.

question: Why is it beneficial to look far ahead while driving on the highway?
options: a:It lets you text safely,b:It reduces the need for last-minute braking or turning,c:It helps you keep up with traffic,d:It allows you to spot upcoming police officers
note: Looking far ahead on the highway helps you spot hazards, slow traffic, and road changes early. This gives you time to adjust your speed or lane smoothly, reducing the need for sudden braking or sharp turns and making your driving safer and more comfortable.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The car ahead stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?
options: a:Pass the vehicle slowly at 10 mph or less.,b:Stop and proceed only after all pedestrians have cleared.,c:Change lanes and cautiously pass the stopped vehicle.,d:Sound your horn and pass on the left.
note: If the car ahead stops at a crosswalk, you must also stop and never pass it. There may be pedestrians in the crosswalk that you cannot see. Wait until all pedestrians have completely crossed and it is clearly safe before you proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far in advance must you signal before turning according to South Carolina law?
options: a:50 feet.,b:150 feet.,c:100 feet.
note: South Carolina law requires you to signal at least 100 feet before turning. This gives other drivers and pedestrians enough time to see your intention and react safely.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, what assumption should you make?
options: a:Expect the parked vehicle to re-enter traffic immediately.,b:Speed up to pass quickly.,c:Assume the driver may open a door into traffic and exercise caution.
note: When passing a parked vehicle, you should assume someone might open a door or pull out suddenly. Slow slightly if needed, leave extra space, and be ready to brake or steer away.

question: If heavy smoke covers the roadway ahead, you should:
options: a:Reduce speed, move as far right as possible, and stop off the roadway.,b:Turn on high beam headlights and continue slowly.,c:Stop in the travel lane until smoke clears.,d:Increase speed to clear the area quickly.
note: If smoke or fog severely limits visibility, slow down, move as far right as you safely can, and stop completely off the roadway. Keep your lights on low beam and hazard lights on so others can see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are turning left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you complete the turn?
options: a:The lane closest to your previous lane.,b:The rightmost lane.,c:Either lane at your discretion.
note: When turning left onto a one‑way street, you must enter the lane closest to the center line or to the lane you turned from. Do not swing wide into another lane during the turn.

question: A red traffic signal requires you to do which of the following?
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection,b:Stop at the stop line,c:All of the above,d:Stop before entering any crosswalk
note: At a steady red light, you must come to a complete stop at the stop line if there is one, before any crosswalk, and before entering the intersection. The law requires you to stop at whichever of these you reach first and remain stopped until the light changes or you are otherwise allowed to proceed.

question: When is highway pavement especially slippery?
options: a:After it has been raining several hours.,b:Only during heavy rainstorms.,c:One to two hours into a rain.,d:Just after it begins to rain.
note: Pavement is most slippery just after rain begins because oil, grease, and dust that have built up on the road mix with the first water and form a slick film. After it has rained for a while, much of this residue is washed away and the surface usually becomes less slippery, though you should still drive with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When completing a pass, how will you know you have enough space to return to your lane?
options: a:The other driver signals you to return.,b:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:You have waited at least five seconds.,d:You can hear the passed vehicle honk.
note: When passing, you need enough space before moving back into your lane so you don’t cut off the other driver. A good rule is to wait until you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle, including both headlights, in your rearview mirror. This indicates you have created a safe following distance before returning to your lane.

question: Is it illegal to drive alongside a motorcycle in the same lane?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, just like any other motor vehicle. Drivers of cars and trucks must not share a lane side‑by‑side with a motorcycle because it leaves the rider with too little space to maneuver or avoid hazards. Always allow a motorcycle the full width of the lane.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, what should you do?
options: a:Look toward the right edge of the road until the vehicle passes.,b:Switch to high beams to see better.,c:Stare directly into the headlights.,d:Flash your lights repeatedly.
note: At night, bright oncoming headlights can temporarily blind you. To reduce glare, briefly look toward the right edge of your lane and use the road edge or lane line as a guide until the vehicle passes. Do not stare directly into the headlights, and do not use your high beams at oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic light turns from green to yellow as you near an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Turn off your headlights.,b:Accelerate to beat the light.,c:Be prepared to stop safely; do not speed up to beat the red.,d:Stop abruptly in the center of the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and be prepared to stop before the intersection if you can do so safely, rather than speeding up to try to beat the red light. Entering on red or stopping abruptly in the intersection is unsafe and often illegal.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and/or siren, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and stay in your lane.,b:Keep driving in your lane.,c:Pull to the right curb or side of the road and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and/or a siren, you must pull as close as safely possible to the right-hand edge or curb of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed. This creates a clear path so the emergency vehicle can move quickly and safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or False: You only need to signal 50 to 75 feet before turning at an intersection in South Carolina.
options: a:Only at night,b:False,c:True,d:Only when other vehicles are present
note: In South Carolina, you must signal continuously for at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes. Signaling only 50 to 75 feet before a turn does not give other road users enough warning and does not meet the legal requirement, so the statement is false.

question: What is true about excessive speed?
options: a:It increases your ability to react to hazards.,b:It reduces the chance of a crash.,c:It often leads to high-risk decision-making and increases crash risk.,d:It is always acceptable if you are an experienced driver.
note: Driving at excessive speed greatly increases crash risk. Higher speeds reduce the time you have to see and react to hazards, increase stopping distance, and make any collision more severe. Speeding often leads to poor decisions, such as unsafe passing or running yellow lights.

question: What is the best way to handle being tailgated?
options: a:Change lanes or gradually slow down to encourage the tailgater to pass,b:Slam on your brakes to make them back off,c:Speed up to get away from the tailgater,d:Yell and gesture to the other driver
note: If you are being tailgated, the safest response is to create space. When it is safe, change lanes to let the tailgater pass, or gradually slow down so they can go around you. Avoid sudden braking or aggressive behavior, which can cause a rear-end crash or escalate conflict.

question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic you should:
options: a:Flash your headlights and speed up to retaliate.,b:Attempt to block their vehicle.,c:Pull alongside and yell at them.,d:Let it go and continue driving safely.
note: If another driver cuts you off, stay calm and avoid reacting aggressively. Do not speed up, block them, or confront them. Instead, slow slightly if needed to re-establish a safe following distance and continue driving defensively. This helps prevent road rage and reduces crash risk.

question: A leaky exhaust system is dangerous because it can cause:
options: a:Loss of hearing.,b:Brake failure.,c:Carbon monoxide poisoning.,d:Increased fuel economy.
note: A leaky exhaust system is dangerous because it can let carbon monoxide leak into the passenger area. Carbon monoxide is a colorless, odorless gas that can quickly cause headache, dizziness, unconsciousness, and death. Any suspected exhaust leak should be repaired immediately and the vehicle should not be driven in enclosed spaces.

question: Which drivers are covered by the South Carolina Point System?
options: a:Only permit holders.,b:Only intermediate drivers.,c:All licensed drivers.,d:Only drivers with prior convictions.
note: All licensed drivers in South Carolina are subject to the point system. When you are convicted of certain traffic violations, points are added to your driving record. Accumulating too many points within a set time period can lead to suspension of your driving privileges.

question: Which foot should you use for both braking and accelerating?
options: a:Left foot for braking and right for accelerating,b:Right foot for both braking and accelerating,c:Either foot for braking,d:Alternate feet to improve reaction time
note: You should use your right foot for both the accelerator and the brake. This helps prevent accidentally pressing both pedals at once and gives you more consistent, controlled movements between speeding up and slowing down.

question: At night, which of these is most difficult to see?
options: a:Traffic lights.,b:Other motorists.,c:Road signs.,d:Pedestrians.
note: At night, pedestrians are usually the hardest to see because they are smaller, often not well lit, and may wear dark clothing. Drivers should use headlights properly, reduce speed in poorly lit areas, and scan carefully for people walking along or crossing the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-way, two-lane street, what must be true before you can pass safely?
options: a:You can see the road ahead clearly and can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.,b:Your vehicle is capable of the speed to pass, regardless of visibility.,c:You have signaled for at least 50 feet.,d:Other drivers wave you on to pass.
note: On a two-way, two-lane road, you may only pass when you can clearly see enough clear roadway ahead, there are no signs or markings prohibiting passing, and you can complete the pass and return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic. Never rely on other drivers waving you on; base your decision on your own clear view and legal passing conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs tell you?
options: a:Suggested safe speeds only for bad weather,b:How fast other drivers are traveling,c:Recommended speeds for heavy traffic,d:The maximum or minimum legal speed allowed on that roadway under ideal conditions
note: Speed limit signs show the maximum (and sometimes minimum) legal speed for that road in ideal conditions. You must still slow down below the posted limit when weather, traffic, or road conditions make the posted speed unsafe.

question: Why is maintaining a space cushion around your vehicle important?
options: a:It prevents distractions from other vehicles.,b:It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.,c:It helps keep traffic flowing faster.
note: A space cushion is the safety gap between your vehicle and others. Keeping this space gives you time and room to see hazards early and react smoothly to sudden stops, swerves, or mistakes by other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking between two vehicles, what is the first maneuver you should make?
options: a:Pull up even with the car ahead of the space you want,b:Turn the wheel to the right immediately,c:Back in at full speed,d:Stop in the middle of the lane
note: For standard parallel parking, after signaling and checking traffic, you first pull up and stop parallel and close to the vehicle in front of the space. From this position you then begin backing into the space while turning the wheel as needed.

question: True or false: Talking or texting on a cell phone while driving will not significantly increase your crash risk.
options: a:False.,b:True.,c:Only true for hands-free phones.,d:Only true when driving slowly.
note: Talking or texting on a phone while driving takes your attention away from the road and greatly increases your chance of a crash. Even hands-free conversations can be distracting, so you should minimize phone use and never text while driving.

question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?
options: a:Only if the emergency vehicle is behind you.,b:When you see flashing lights or hear a siren.,c:Only if another vehicle yields first.,d:Under no circumstances.
note: You must yield to emergency vehicles using a siren and/or flashing lights by pulling to the right side of the road and stopping when safe. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless a police officer directs you otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Only at uncontrolled intersections.,b:Whenever yielding helps prevent a collision.,c:Never — you always have the right-of-way.
note: Right-of-way is never absolute. Even if the law says you have the right-of-way, you must yield whenever doing so will help prevent a collision. Safe driving means being willing to let others go first if it avoids a crash.

question: How can you help the driver behind you keep a safe following distance?
options: a:Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,b:Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.,c:Maintain a steady speed and signal early for maneuvers.
note: Keeping a steady speed and signaling early for turns, lane changes, or slowing helps the driver behind you judge distance and react smoothly. Sudden speed changes or late signals make it harder for them to maintain a safe following distance.

question: Is holding a driver license a right or a privilege?
options: a:A requirement,b:A privilege,c:A right,d:A guarantee
note: In the United States, driving is a privilege, not a guaranteed right. You must meet licensing requirements, obey traffic laws, and can lose your license if you violate those laws or become unsafe to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Stop and wait for the light to change.,b:Proceed through the intersection with caution.,c:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. Be prepared to yield to pedestrians and cross traffic if necessary.

question: Why is night driving more hazardous?
options: a:Distance and vehicle speeds are harder to judge in the dark.,b:The speed limit is increased at night.,c:There are always fewer vehicles on the road at night.
note: Night driving is more dangerous because you cannot see as far or as clearly, making it harder to judge other vehicles’ distance and speed. Your headlights limit how much of the road you can see, so hazards may appear with less warning.

question: A solid white line down the center of a two-lane road indicates:
options: a:A center turn lane is present.,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction and lane changes are discouraged or prohibited.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is allowed.,d:A pedestrian-only zone.
note: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line between lanes means you should stay in your lane; lane changes and passing are discouraged and may be prohibited in some areas, such as near intersections or in tunnels.

question: What must you do when a school bus is stopped ahead with lights flashing and its stop arm extended?
options: a:Proceed only if you are on the opposite side of a divided highway with a physical median or barrier.,b:Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,c:Do not change lanes and do not pass while the red lights are flashing and the stop arm is extended.,d:Stop regardless of whether you see children in the road whenever the red lights are flashing and the stop arm is extended.
note: When a school bus has red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. On a divided highway with a physical median, only traffic traveling in the same direction as the bus must stop; on undivided roads, traffic in both directions must stop.

question: For drivers under 21, at what BAC can the license be suspended?
options: a:0.08 percent or more.,b:Any detectable amount of alcohol.,c:0.15 percent or more.
note: Many states, including South Carolina, have zero-tolerance laws for drivers under 21. Any detectable amount of alcohol in the system can lead to penalties such as license suspension, even if the BAC is below the adult legal limit of 0.08 percent.

question: What do yellow lines on the roadway separate?
options: a:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,b:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.,c:Carpool lanes from regular lanes.,d:Bike lanes from vehicle lanes.
note: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads. A single or double yellow centerline helps drivers know where the middle of the road is and when passing is allowed or prohibited.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When exiting an expressway or when conditions require more time to react.,b:When following a motorcycle, bicycle, or any vehicle that could stop quickly.,c:When behind a large vehicle that blocks your vision or in any situation where you need extra time and space to react.
note: You should increase your following distance whenever conditions make it harder to see or stop in time. This includes when following large vehicles that block your view, in bad weather, in heavy traffic, when following motorcycles or bicycles, when exiting an expressway, or when you are being tailgated.

question: If it begins to sleet or snow while you are driving, you should:
options: a:All of the above,b:Keep your windshield and mirrors clear,c:Allow additional following distance from the vehicle ahead,d:Approach other vehicles with extra caution
note: In sleet or snow you should do all of the following: keep your windshield and mirrors clear for visibility, increase your following distance to allow more stopping time, and approach other vehicles with extra caution because traction and control are reduced. All of these actions together help you drive more safely in winter conditions.

question: Why should you not make sudden stops in front of large trucks or buses?
options: a:They need longer distances to stop due to their size and weight.,b:Truck drivers can always stop quickly.,c:Because large vehicles travel slower than passenger cars.,d:Small vehicles are easier to see behind trucks.
note: Large trucks and buses are much heavier than passenger cars and need a longer distance to stop, even with good brakes. If you stop suddenly in front of them, they may not be able to stop in time, which can cause a serious rear‑end collision. Always avoid cutting closely in front of large vehicles and leave extra space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signals?
options: a:Only when pulling next to the curb.,b:Only when pulling away from the curb.,c:When pulling next to or away from the curb.
note: You must signal any time you change your position on the road, including when you pull toward a curb to park and when you pull away from the curb to reenter traffic. Signaling both movements lets other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know what you intend to do so they can react safely.

question: What should you do on slippery roads?
options: a:Always drive at the posted limit even if conditions are poor.,b:Brake sharply to test traction.,c:Slow down.,d:Drive faster to get through the area quickly.
note: On slippery roads from rain, snow, or ice, you should slow down to maintain traction and control. Lower speeds reduce the chance of skidding and give you more time and distance to stop or steer around hazards.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is correct?
options: a:No drugs affect driving if taken in small amounts.,b:Prescription drugs are always safe if you feel alert.,c:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.,d:Only illegal drugs impair your driving.
note: Many drugs, including over‑the‑counter cold medicines, allergy pills, and prescription medications, can make you drowsy, dizzy, or slow your reactions. It is illegal and unsafe to drive when any drug impairs your ability, even if the drug is legal or prescribed. Always read labels and follow medical advice before driving.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Never pass them under any circumstances.,b:Avoid driving alongside large vehicles and do not tailgate.,c:Flash your lights to make them aware of you.,d:Drive as close as possible to their rear bumper.
note: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots along their sides and directly behind them. To stay visible, avoid driving right next to them for long periods and never follow too closely. Leave extra space so the driver can see you in their mirrors and you have room to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, besides checking mirrors, what should you do?
options: a:Always slow down in your current lane.,b:Never look over your right shoulder.,c:Glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
note: Before changing lanes, you must check your mirrors and then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This shoulder check lets you see the blind spot that mirrors cannot cover and helps you avoid vehicles that may be hidden there.

question: Which of the following is a common cause of crashes?
options: a:Driving too fast for conditions,b:Consistently checking mirrors and blind spots,c:Always yielding the right-of-way,d:Using seat belts properly
note: Driving too fast for conditions is a major cause of crashes. Even if you are at or below the posted speed limit, you must slow down when roads are wet, icy, foggy, or crowded. Safe speed depends on visibility, traffic, and road surface, not just the number on the sign.

question: After a minor intersection collision with no injuries, what should you do?
options: a:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if possible.,b:Leave vehicles in the traffic lane until police arrive.,c:Immediately drive away from the scene.,d:Walk away from the vehicles and leave them.
note: After a minor crash with no injuries, and if the vehicles can be moved, you should pull them out of the traffic lane to a safe spot such as the shoulder or a nearby parking area. This helps prevent additional collisions, keeps traffic flowing, and allows everyone to exchange information safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you do?
options: a:Make a U-turn through the median to reach your exit.,b:Stop and back up to your exit.,c:Continue to the next exit and re-route safely.
note: If you miss your freeway exit, keep going to the next exit. Never stop, back up, or make a U-turn on the freeway or in the median. Continuing to the next exit and re-routing is the only safe and legal option.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roundabout, to whom should you yield?
options: a:Only to cars,b:Any crossing pedestrians and bicyclists as well as traffic already in the roundabout.,c:Only vehicles inside the roundabout.
note: At a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing at the entrances and exits, and to all vehicles already circulating in the roundabout. Enter only when there is a safe gap in traffic.

question: A broken yellow centerline indicates:
options: a:Passing is prohibited for both directions.,b:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:The road is one-way.,d:Passing on the right is required.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means you may pass on the left when there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe and legal to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action is prohibited when changing lanes?
options: a:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,b:Cross the centerline in an intersection.,c:Check your blind spots by looking over your left or right shoulder.
note: You must never change lanes by crossing the centerline within an intersection. Lane changes should be made before or after the intersection, and only after checking mirrors and blind spots by looking over your shoulder to be sure the lane is clear.

question: When another driver is passing you, what should you do?
options: a:Maintain your speed and position while being on guard and allow space if they need to return to your lane.,b:Speed up to prevent them passing.,c:Move out of the lane immediately regardless of conditions.
note: When another driver is passing you, stay in your lane and maintain a steady speed so they can judge their pass safely. Be prepared for unexpected actions and allow space for the passing vehicle to return to your lane if needed.

question: Compared to daytime driving, driving at night is:
options: a:Safe if you use high beams always.,b:More dangerous due to reduced visibility and other factors.,c:Less dangerous.,d:No different.
note: Driving at night is more dangerous because you cannot see as far, it is harder to judge distances and speeds, glare can reduce visibility, and there is a higher chance of encountering fatigued or impaired drivers.

question: On a four-lane roadway, must you stop for a stopped school bus when you are traveling in the opposite direction?
options: a:True (you do not need to stop when traveling opposite on a divided four-lane),b:False
note: On a four‑lane road that is not divided by a physical barrier or unpaved median, drivers in both directions must stop for a school bus with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended. You are excused from stopping only when you are on the opposite side of a clearly divided highway (such as a raised median, barrier, or unpaved strip). If it is simply a painted center line on a four‑lane road, you must stop even when traveling in the opposite direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what is your required action?
options: a:Yield to cross traffic that is close enough to cause a conflict.,b:Always stop before proceeding no matter what.,c:Yield only to vehicles on your right.
note: At a yield sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop, yielding the right‑of‑way to any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection or close enough to be a hazard. If there is no conflicting traffic, you may proceed without stopping.

question: At a railroad crossing, what must you be sure to do?
options: a:Only look for trains coming from one direction.,b:Rely on crossing gates alone to indicate a train is coming.,c:Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings and be cautious of multiple trains.
note: At railroad crossings, always look and listen for trains coming from either direction and be prepared to stop. Watch for vehicles that must stop at all crossings, such as school buses and vehicles carrying hazardous materials. Never assume the tracks are clear just because the gates are up or lights are off; check carefully for more than one train.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection blocked by traffic ahead, you should:
options: a:Move forward slowly to keep traffic flowing.,b:Stay out of the intersection until you can clear it.,c:Get as close to the car ahead as possible.,d:Enter the intersection and wait.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless there is enough space on the other side for your vehicle to completely clear it. Entering when traffic is stopped ahead can leave you blocking the intersection, which is illegal and can prevent cross traffic and emergency vehicles from passing.

question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line means:
options: a:No passing is allowed from either direction.,b:Passing is permitted only on the right.,c:Traffic next to the broken line may pass; traffic next to the solid line may not.,d:Both directions may pass freely.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the broken line, and only when it is safe. Traffic on the side with the solid yellow line must not cross it to pass.

question: When changing lanes, how can drivers see objects in their blind spots?
options: a:Look over the left or right shoulder toward the blind spot.,b:Trust the outside mirror only.,c:Use the inside rearview mirror only.,d:Flash headlights to make other vehicles visible.
note: Blind spots cannot be seen with mirrors alone. Look over your shoulder toward the lane you plan to enter to check blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle in the same direction, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can no longer see the vehicle behind you,b:Immediately after passing,c:After about three seconds,d:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror
note: Do not return to your lane until you can clearly see the passed vehicle's front in your rearview mirror and it is safe to do so.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:You should speed up to make the turn before the light changes.,b:You do not need to signal to turn from the indicated lane.,c:The green arrow protection is ending; prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turning time is ending; yield to oncoming traffic and prepare to stop.

question: What following distance should you maintain under normal driving conditions?
options: a:At least a three- to four-second gap.,b:One-second gap.,c:Following distance is only important on snow and ice.
note: Under normal conditions keep at least a three- to four-second following distance; increase it for adverse weather, higher speeds, or heavy traffic.

question: When must headlights be used?
options: a:When parking on the shoulder,b:Only after 7 p.m. and before 7 a.m.,c:Only during heavy rain,d:From a half hour after sunset until a half hour before sunrise and whenever visibility is reduced
note: Use headlights from one‑half hour after sunset to one‑half hour before sunrise, and any time visibility is poor (such as in rain, fog, or snow) so you can see and be seen by other road users.

question: What does a single dashed yellow line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.,b:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,c:Passing is prohibited for both directions.,d:It marks a bike lane.
note: A single dashed yellow line in the center of the road separates traffic moving in opposite directions. When the line is dashed, drivers in both directions may cross it to pass if there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe and legal to do so.

question: If you suffer a tire blowout while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Tap or pump the brakes to slow down.,b:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly to stop immediately.,c:Slow down gradually and avoid braking until the vehicle has slowed.
note: In a tire blowout, hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Avoid braking hard; braking suddenly can cause you to lose control. Once the vehicle has slowed and is stable, steer to a safe place off the road and stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive much slower than the normal flow of traffic, what may be required?
options: a:You always retain the right-of-way.,b:Pull off the road and let other vehicles pass if you are causing traffic to back up.,c:You should refuse to let others pass.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can create a hazard by causing other drivers to brake or make sudden lane changes. On two-lane roads, if several vehicles are lined up behind you, you may be required to pull off at a safe place and let them pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you NOT do?
options: a:Back up on the road or shoulder.,b:Proceed to the next exit and find a safe route to your destination.,c:Continue on the freeway and find an alternate route.
note: If you miss your exit on a freeway, you must never back up on the travel lanes or the shoulder because fast-moving traffic may not expect a vehicle reversing. Instead, continue to the next exit, leave the freeway safely, and then find a route back to your intended destination.

question: If dust or smoke reduces your visibility, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and turn on your headlights.,b:Turn on parking lights only.,c:Turn on your emergency flashers.
note: When dust or smoke reduces visibility, slow down and turn on your low-beam headlights so you can see and be seen. If visibility becomes so poor that you cannot drive safely, pull completely off the road and stop. Parking lights alone are not sufficient, and emergency flashers are typically used only when stopped or moving very slowly in an emergency.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Merging traffic.,b:Pedestrian crossing.,c:Proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow traffic signal means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield to other vehicles, pedestrians, or hazards.

question: When you see a 'Merging traffic' sign on the freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Always remain at your present speed regardless of traffic.,b:Honk at incoming traffic to warn them.,c:Make room for entering vehicles by changing lanes if it is safe to do so.
note: When you see a merging traffic sign on a freeway or multi‑lane road, you should help entering vehicles merge safely. If possible, change lanes away from the merge area or adjust your speed to create a safe gap, while still obeying speed limits and checking mirrors and blind spots.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Bad weather,b:Mechanical failure,c:Human error,d:New drivers
note: Most crashes are caused by human error, such as inattention, distraction, misjudging speed or distance, or failing to yield. Weather and mechanical problems do contribute to some crashes, but they are far less common than driver mistakes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statements about driving speed are true?
options: a:Speed has no impact on fatality risk.,b:Higher speeds increase the chance of fatality and you should increase following distance at higher speeds.,c:Faster speeds always reduce stopping distance.,d:Speed has no effect on stopping distance.
note: As your speed increases, both your stopping distance and the severity of any collision increase. Because it takes longer to see, react, and stop at higher speeds, you must leave more following distance to have enough time and space to avoid hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At what speed should you travel relative to conditions and other vehicles?
options: a:At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions and within the posted limit.,b:Always at the posted speed limit regardless of conditions.,c:Always at the speed of surrounding vehicles no matter what.,d:At the maximum possible speed for your vehicle.
note: You must always choose a speed that is safe for current road, traffic, and weather conditions and that does not exceed the posted speed limit. In rain, fog, heavy traffic, or other poor conditions, you are required to slow down even if that means driving below the posted limit.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what is the best course of action?
options: a:Lay down in your car and go to sleep,b:Walk into the road to flag down drivers,c:Get out of the car and go for help,d:Stay in your car and wait for help
note: If you are stranded in a snowstorm, you should usually stay with your vehicle. The car provides shelter from the cold and is much easier for rescuers to see than a person on foot. Run the engine only periodically to conserve fuel and prevent carbon monoxide buildup by keeping the exhaust pipe clear of snow. Use hazard lights, dome light, or bright cloth to signal for help rather than walking into the storm.

question: What can occur if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or OTC medicine?
options: a:The medicine always blocks alcohol's effects.,b:The combination can multiply the impairing effects of alcohol or the medicine.,c:Alcohol helps medicines work better.,d:No interaction occurs.
note: Alcohol can interact with many prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines in a way that increases drowsiness, slows reaction time, and impairs judgment. The combination can be more dangerous than either substance alone and can seriously affect your ability to drive safely.

question: When operating near a large commercial vehicle, you should:
options: a:Drive on its right side on hills and curves.,b:Always pass immediately.,c:Avoid driving beside it for long periods.,d:Follow closely to reduce wind drag.
note: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots along both sides, especially on the right. If you drive beside them for a long time, the driver may not see you and could change lanes into your path. Pass safely and promptly, and avoid lingering next to large commercial vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it permissible to drive on the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:When the vehicle ahead is turning left.,b:Only if the shoulder is wide enough.,c:If traffic is stopped ahead.,d:Never; do not pass on the shoulder.
note: You must not drive on the shoulder to pass another vehicle. The shoulder is for emergencies and stopped vehicles, not for travel or passing. Other drivers do not expect moving traffic there and may pull onto the shoulder suddenly, creating a serious crash risk.

question: When stopped for a traffic violation or during an equipment check, what must a driver produce if requested?
options: a:Proof of registration.,b:Proof of insurance.,c:Their driver license.
note: When stopped by law enforcement, you are generally required to show your driver license, proof of vehicle registration, and proof of financial responsibility (insurance) upon request. Keeping these documents readily available in the vehicle helps the stop go smoothly and ensures you are complying with state law.

question: If an aggressive driver is tailgating you, you should:
options: a:Brake-check them.,b:Speed up to increase the gap.,c:Stare at the driver as they pass.,d:Make every effort to get out of their way.
note: If someone is tailgating you, stay calm and avoid any actions that could escalate the situation, such as brake-checking or making eye contact. When it is safe, change lanes or otherwise allow the aggressive driver to pass. Your goal is to create space and reduce risk, not to punish or confront the other driver.

question: After an accident you should:
options: a:Report the accident the following week.,b:Leave the scene and call your insurance company from home.,c:Protect the area,d:Only exchange insurance information if requested.
note: After a collision, you must stop at or near the scene, prevent further crashes if you can do so safely, and protect the area by turning on hazard lights, setting out flares or warning triangles if available, and moving vehicles out of traffic when appropriate. Then check for injuries, call 911 or law enforcement, exchange information, and report the crash as required by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian?
options: a:Only when pedestrians signal you to stop.,b:To any pedestrian crossing a street in a marked or unmarked crosswalk.,c:Only to pedestrians in marked crosswalks.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in both marked and unmarked crosswalks. An unmarked crosswalk typically exists at most intersections, even if there are no painted lines. For safety, be prepared to yield to pedestrians crossing the road anywhere, especially where visibility is limited or people are clearly attempting to cross.

question: When driving in fog, is using your high beam headlights recommended?
options: a:True,b:False
note: In fog, use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams, and fog lights if your vehicle has them, help you see the road and help others see you without creating extra glare.

question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must drivers do?
options: a:Assume the guard's directions are optional.,b:Copy what surrounding traffic does instead.,c:Follow the crossing guard's directions.
note: A crossing guard’s instructions must be obeyed just like those of a traffic signal or police officer. In school zones, follow the guard’s hand signals and stop signs, even if they differ from the normal traffic light, to protect children and other pedestrians crossing the street.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should the maximum posted speed limit be driven?
options: a:Only under ideal driving conditions,b:Only at night,c:Only during the day,d:Whenever traffic is heavy
note: The posted maximum speed is the fastest you are allowed to drive only when conditions are ideal: good visibility, dry pavement, light traffic, and a safe vehicle. If conditions are less than ideal—such as rain, fog, heavy traffic, or poor road surfaces—you must drive slower than the posted maximum so you can stop safely and maintain control.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When it may help prevent a collision.,b:To express annoyance at a slow driver.,c:Whenever another vehicle is in your way.
note: Use your horn to alert other road users when it may help prevent a collision or warn of a hazard, such as when another driver is about to move into your lane without seeing you. Do not use the horn to express anger, impatience, or just because someone is in your way; unnecessary horn use can startle others and create unsafe situations.

question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?
options: a:Activate your four-way flashers and continue at the same speed.,b:Increase your speed to avoid impeding traffic.,c:Stay alert, slow down, and obey all work-zone signs and flaggers.
note: In work zones you must slow down, stay alert, and be prepared for sudden changes such as lane shifts, workers near the roadway, and construction vehicles entering or leaving. Always obey the posted work-zone speed limits, signs, and any directions from flaggers, and increase your following distance to allow more time to react.

question: Approaching an octagonal sign means you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop.,b:Slow and proceed without stopping.,c:Yield only to oncoming traffic.,d:Turn left.
note: An octagonal (eight-sided) red sign is always a STOP sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then yield to pedestrians and other traffic before proceeding when it is safe.

question: When you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle using its siren or lights, what must you do?
options: a:Drive to the right side of the road and stop until it passes.,b:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.,c:Slow to a stop in your lane and wave it on.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using its siren and/or flashing lights, you must immediately yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping until it has passed. If you are in an intersection, clear the intersection first, then pull to the right and stop. Do not stop in the middle of your lane or wave the vehicle around you.

question: Which method checks a blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Use the inside rearview mirror only.,b:Sound your horn.,c:Use only the side mirror.,d:Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Before changing lanes, you must briefly turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction of the lane you want to enter to make sure no vehicle is in your blind spot.

question: Which statement about a work zone is correct?
options: a:Drivers do not need to slow down in work zones.,b:They are marked with black and white signs.,c:Work zones may be stationary or moving and are marked with orange signs; drivers must slow down.
note: Work zones are marked with orange signs and may be stationary (like road repairs) or moving (like line painting or mowing). Drivers must slow down, obey posted work zone speed limits, and be prepared for workers, equipment, and sudden stops.

question: What color are pavement markings that separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Blue,b:Yellow,c:White,d:Red
note: Yellow pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions, such as the centerline on a two‑way road. White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.

question: When a school bus is stopped with its stop arm extended, drivers should:
options: a:Proceed when they think children have finished crossing.,b:Honk to warn children before passing on the left.,c:Come to a complete stop and wait until the stop arm is withdrawn.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, drivers in most situations must come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, and it is clearly safe to proceed.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to law enforcement?
options: a:Only if you are in an accident.,b:Only if you are stopped and cited.,c:If stopped for a citation or involved in a collision.
note: You must carry proof of financial responsibility (usually an insurance card) whenever you drive and show it to law enforcement when requested, such as if you are stopped for a traffic violation or involved in a collision.

question: If you approach a railroad crossing and see no train, when must you still stop?
options: a:If the crossing lights are flashing.,b:If the crossing gate is lowered.,c:If a stop sign is posted.,d:All of the above.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing any time a stop sign is posted, the crossing lights are flashing, the gate is down or coming down, or a flagger directs you to stop—even if you do not see a train. These controls mean a train may be approaching or the crossing is not safe to enter.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to turn right, what is the safest action?
options: a:Try to squeeze between the vehicle and the curb,b:Pass on the right between the truck and curb,c:Quickly turn before the truck completes its turn,d:Wait until the truck or bus has completed its turn before you turn
note: Large trucks and buses often swing wide or start a turn from another lane to complete a right turn. Never try to squeeze between them and the curb or rush ahead of them. Wait until the truck or bus has fully completed the turn before you make your right turn.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Keep the wheels straight ahead.,b:Turn the wheels to the left toward the center of the road.,c:Turn the wheels to the right toward the curb.
note: When parking downhill on a two-way street with a curb, turn your front wheels toward the curb (to the right). If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will hit the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: What do your brake lights communicate to other drivers?
options: a:You are making a turn,b:You are changing lanes,c:You are slowing down or stopping,d:Your emergency brake is on
note: Brake lights warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down or stopping. This gives them time to reduce speed and maintain a safe following distance, helping to prevent rear-end collisions.

question: Which behavior is a common sign of impaired (drunk) driving?
options: a:Weaving between lanes.,b:Driving consistently with traffic flow.,c:Using turn signals properly.
note: Weaving between lanes is a classic sign of impaired driving. Alcohol and drugs affect judgment, coordination, and reaction time, which can cause drifting, weaving, sudden braking, inconsistent speeds, and other erratic movements.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips on the road?
options: a:Through sound and vibration they warn inattentive drivers that their vehicle is leaving the travel lane.,b:They help test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,c:They alert drivers to potential tire problems.
note: Rumble strips are grooved or raised patterns on the road that create noise and vibration when you drive over them. This alerts inattentive or drowsy drivers that they are drifting out of their lane or approaching a hazard, giving them time to correct their path.

question: Drivers are prohibited from passing a school bus when its red lights are flashing:
options: a:Only on two-lane roads.,b:True.,c:False.,d:Only during school hours.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, drivers in most situations must stop and may not pass until the lights stop flashing and the bus moves or the driver signals you to proceed. Some states allow passing on the opposite side of a divided highway, but the general safety rule is that flashing red lights mean you must stop, not pass.

question: Before driving while taking medication, what should you do?
options: a:Consult your doctor or pharmacist about possible driving effects,b:Have someone follow you home,c:Leave your windows open while driving,d:Take an extra dose to stay alert
note: Many prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines can make you drowsy, slow your reactions, or affect your judgment. Before driving, you should ask your doctor or pharmacist whether a medication can affect your ability to drive safely and follow their advice about driving or dosage timing.

question: If a fire engine is following you on a two-lane street but has no lights or siren on, how should you respond?
options: a:Speed up to get out of its way.,b:Stop immediately as quickly as possible.,c:Continue driving normally.
note: You are required to yield and pull over only when an emergency vehicle is using its lights and/or siren. If a fire engine is behind you with no lights or siren, treat it like any other vehicle: obey the speed limit, maintain a safe following distance, and continue driving normally.

question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Checking antifreeze and washer fluid is important.,b:Using snow tires can improve traction.,c:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,d:Using cruise control in winter is safe.
note: Cruise control should not be used on snow, ice, or in other slippery or hazardous conditions because it can cause you to lose control if the tires start to skid. In winter, you should check antifreeze and washer fluid, consider snow tires for better traction, and drive with extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the road center has a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line with the broken line next to your lane, you may:
options: a:Pass if traffic ahead is clear.,b:Pass only in an emergency.,c:Never pass under any condition.,d:Pass only during daylight hours.
note: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means only the side with the broken line may pass. If the broken line is on your side, you may cross it to pass when the lane is clear and it is safe, and there is no oncoming traffic.

question: How would you describe backing (reversing) a vehicle?
options: a:Dangerous only in large vehicles.,b:Always dangerous because it's hard to see behind the vehicle.,c:Dangerous only when you have a helper.,d:Always risky because your view to the rear and sides is limited; back slowly and check carefully.
note: Backing is always risky because your view to the rear and sides is limited, even with mirrors or cameras. You should back slowly, check around the vehicle before moving, and use a helper when possible to reduce blind spots and avoid hitting people or objects.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs traffic to go through a red light without stopping, what should you do?
options: a:Refuse and wait for the light to change.,b:Follow the officer's directions and go through the intersection.,c:Obey the red light and stop until it turns green.
note: A police officer directing traffic has authority over traffic signals and signs. When an officer tells you to proceed through a red light, you must follow the officer’s directions, proceeding carefully through the intersection as instructed.

question: If you must drive in fog, you should use:
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Only parking lights.,d:Interior dome lights.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and create glare, which makes it harder to see. Low beams help you see the road and help others see you without increasing glare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, you and another vehicle arrive at the same time and the other vehicle is on your right. What should you do?
options: a:Increase speed and hurry through the intersection.,b:Yield to the vehicle on your right and wait.,c:Enter the intersection forcing the other vehicle to stop.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. If the other vehicle is on your right, you should wait and allow that vehicle to go first.

question: If your wheels run off the pavement, what is the correct recovery technique?
options: a:Hit the brakes hard and jerk the steering wheel back onto the road.,b:Grip the wheel,c:Stop in place and wait for help.,d:Immediately swerve back onto the pavement at speed.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, ease off the accelerator, and slow down gradually. Once the vehicle is under control and your speed is reduced, gently steer back onto the pavement when it is safe. Sudden braking or jerking the wheel can cause you to lose control or skid.

question: At a railroad crossing that has only a crossbuck and no gates or lights, how should you proceed?
options: a:Only proceed if another driver waves you on,b:Turn up your radio to better hear approaching trains,c:Cross quickly without stopping,d:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming
note: At a crossing with only a crossbuck and no gates or lights, you must treat it as an uncontrolled crossing: slow down, look and listen carefully in both directions, and be prepared to stop. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks completely. Obey any flagger if present.

question: Which statement about backing on a roadway is correct?
options: a:Drivers should look behind them and check traffic before and while backing.,b:Drivers should look straight ahead while backing.,c:Traffic checks are not necessary when backing.,d:Only use mirrors when backing.
note: When backing, you must check behind your vehicle before moving and continue to look to the rear while backing. Turn your head and look over your shoulder, using mirrors as a supplement, not a substitute. Always make sure the path is clear of traffic, pedestrians, and obstacles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following about left turns is correct?
options: a:Swing wide into the right lane while turning left.,b:Always finish a left turn onto a four-lane roadway in the far right lane.,c:Complete a left turn into the legal lane nearest your previous lane.
note: For a standard left turn, you should enter and complete the turn into the legal lane nearest to the center line or nearest to the lane you came from, unless signs or lane markings direct otherwise. Swinging wide into other lanes can surprise other drivers and is unsafe.

question: Which driving skills are impaired by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Both alertness and coordination.,b:Coordination.,c:None of the above.,d:Alertness.
note: Alcohol and many drugs impair multiple driving skills at the same time, including alertness, coordination, judgment, and reaction time. Because both alertness and coordination are affected, you are less able to notice hazards and less able to control the vehicle smoothly and quickly.

question: You must exercise extreme caution and yield to children playing in the street:
options: a:True.,b:False.,c:Only near schools.,d:Only if signs are posted.
note: You must always use extra caution around children near the roadway. Children can be unpredictable and may suddenly run into the street, so you should slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield to them whether or not you are near a school or see warning signs.

question: Regarding speed control in curves, what is most important?
options: a:Increase speed before entering the curve to maintain momentum.,b:Slow down before you enter the curve.,c:Drive at the posted speed entering the curve and then slow at the sharpest part.
note: You should slow down before entering a curve, then maintain a safe, steady speed through it. Braking hard in the middle of a curve can cause loss of control, especially at higher speeds. Entering too fast makes it harder to stay in your lane and react to hazards.

question: Approximately how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer need to stop from 55 mph?
options: a:125 feet,b:400 feet,c:50 feet
note: Large trucks need much more distance to stop than passenger cars. A fully loaded tractor‑trailer traveling about 55 mph may need roughly 400 feet or more to come to a complete stop, depending on conditions. Never cut closely in front of a truck because it may not be able to stop in time.

question: How should you adjust your driving on gravel or dirt roads?
options: a:Brake hard in turns for better control,b:Expect better visibility than on pavement,c:Drive at the same speed as on pavement,d:Slow down because you have less traction than on pavement
note: On gravel or dirt roads, your tires have less traction and your stopping distance increases. You should slow down, avoid sudden steering or hard braking, and increase your following distance to maintain control on the loose surface.

question: If you are involved in a collision, what should you do first?
options: a:Leave the scene and call your insurance company,b:Drive to the nearest service station,c:Report the accident to the police within one week,d:Remain near the scene
note: If you are involved in a collision, you must stop and remain at or near the scene. First, check for injuries and call emergency services if needed. If possible, move vehicles out of traffic, turn on hazard lights, and then exchange information and report the crash as required by law. Leaving the scene is illegal in most situations.

question: What effect does even a small amount of alcohol have on driving abilities?
options: a:Alcohol affects only balance,b:Only levels above the legal limit have any effect.,c:Even the smallest amount can reduce concentration,d:Alcohol improves alertness.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair attention, perception, judgment, and memory; no amount is safe for driving.

question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?
options: a:Slow down immediately.,b:You may not pass from your direction of travel.,c:You may pass with caution.,d:The lane is for buses only.
note: A solid yellow line next to your lane indicates passing is prohibited from your direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to change lanes, you should first:
options: a:Start signaling only after you begin the lane change.,b:Check your side and rearview mirrors and signal about 100 feet before changing lanes.,c:Rely only on your mirrors and avoid turning your head.,d:Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.
