note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors, signal in advance, and then quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving. Signaling about 100 feet ahead is a common guideline in lower‑speed areas, but the key is to signal early enough for others to react and always combine mirror checks with a head check.

question: Is it unlawful for a car to try to share a lane with a motorcycle?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a traffic lane. A car must not try to share a lane with a motorcycle.

question: When parking uphill on a roadway with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn them toward the center of the road (left).,b:Turn them toward the side of the road (right).,c:Keep them straight ahead.
note: On an uphill without a curb, turn your wheels toward the road's edge so a rollback will not move into traffic.

question: If you are being tailgated and cannot change lanes, what is the correct response?
options: a:Wait until the way ahead is clear and then gradually reduce speed to encourage the tailgater to pass.,b:Brake sharply to scare the tailgater off.,c:Speed up to put distance between you.,d:Immediately pull to the left shoulder and stop.
note: If you are being tailgated and cannot safely change lanes, keep a steady pace and, when the road ahead is clear, gradually reduce your speed. This increases the following distance in front of you and encourages the tailgater to pass when it becomes safe. Never brake suddenly to “teach them a lesson,” and do not speed up, because both actions increase the risk of a rear-end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is unlawful regarding passing?
options: a:Passing on multi-lane highways when lanes permit.,b:Passing only when it is safe.,c:Passing another vehicle in any marked no-passing zone or over a railroad crossing.
note: Passing is only legal where it is clearly permitted and safe. It is unlawful to pass in any marked no‑passing zone, over or within a short distance of a railroad crossing, on hills or curves where you cannot see far enough ahead, or when there is a solid yellow line on your side of the road. You may pass on multi‑lane roads only when lane markings and conditions allow it and you can do so safely.

question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, what should you do?
options: a:Slowly go around the gates if traffic is heavy.,b:Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.,c:Come to a complete stop behind the gates and wait until they are raised and it is safe to proceed.
note: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you must stop before the gate and wait. Do not drive around or under the gates, even if you do not see a train coming. Trains are often closer and moving faster than they appear, and signals may activate before you can see the train. Proceed only after the gates are fully raised, the lights stop flashing, and you have checked that the tracks are clear.

question: What do double solid yellow lane markings mean?
options: a:Only trucks may pass.,b:Both directions may pass.,c:Neither direction may pass.,d:The lane to the right may pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines between lanes of traffic mean that vehicles traveling in either direction are not allowed to pass or cross the lines to overtake another vehicle. You must stay in your lane and may only cross these lines when making a permitted left turn into or out of a driveway or side road, if state law allows, but not for passing.

question: When entering your parked vehicle you should:
options: a:Look around for obstacles or hazards before entering.,b:Enter only from the passenger side.,c:Signal traffic to stop so you can open your door.,d:Open the trunk first.
note: Before entering your parked vehicle, walk around it and look for obstacles, children, pedestrians, or other hazards that could be in your path. Check the traffic side carefully before opening the door so you do not step into the path of approaching vehicles or cyclists. This habit helps prevent collisions and injuries before you even start driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes you should:
options: a:Signal only after starting the lane change.,b:Rely entirely on your mirrors.,c:Signal at least 500 feet before residential lane changes.,d:Check mirrors, signal, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, signal in advance (about 100 feet before the lane change in residential areas), then quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving. Never rely only on mirrors and never signal after you start moving into the new lane.

question: True or false: Work zones on highways have become increasingly safe for workers and drivers.
options: a:Only under police supervision.,b:Only on rural highways.,c:False.,d:True.
note: Work zones are still dangerous areas for both workers and drivers. Crashes and serious injuries continue to occur in these areas, so you must slow down, obey all signs and flaggers, and stay alert whenever you drive through a work zone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic is approaching while you plan a three-point turnabout, what should you do?
options: a:Begin the turnabout quickly to beat the traffic,b:Flash your headlights and start immediately,c:Yield to all approaching traffic before starting the turnabout,d:Signal and proceed without checking for traffic
note: A three‑point turn should only be done when you have clear space and enough time to complete it safely. If any traffic is approaching from either direction, you must wait and yield until the roadway is clear before starting the maneuver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement is true about driving too slowly?
options: a:Driving too slowly is never unsafe.,b:Speed does not affect safety.,c:It is always safer to drive slower than traffic.,d:Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can be dangerous because it forces other drivers to brake suddenly or make risky lane changes and passing maneuvers. On some roads there are minimum speed limits, and you must not drive so slowly that you interfere with normal, safe traffic movement.

question: The term 'No zone' refers to:
options: a:Blind spots around a truck or bus.,b:A special reduced-speed area.,c:A roadway with restricted radio volume.,d:A designated no-parking zone.
note: A 'No‑zone' is the large blind spot area around trucks and buses where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. These areas are along both sides, directly behind, and sometimes directly in front of the vehicle. Avoid lingering in these zones so the truck or bus driver can see you and react safely.

question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, what is the best practice?
options: a:Start driving and look up directions on the road,b:Depend only on road signs while driving,c:Plan your trip in advance,d:Only have a vague idea of your destination
note: Planning your trip before you drive—by checking a map, GPS, or written directions—reduces the need to look away from the road and make last‑second decisions. This helps you stay focused on traffic and hazards instead of trying to figure out where to go while driving.

question: How can you prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Use high beams in the rain.,b:Drive faster over puddles to clear water.,c:Shift into neutral when entering water.,d:Keep tires with good tread and proper inflation
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. Keeping tires properly inflated, with good tread depth, and driving at lower speeds in wet conditions greatly reduces the risk. Sudden speed changes or driving fast through water make hydroplaning more likely.

question: What is the penalty for refusing a chemical test when requested by law enforcement in South Carolina?
options: a:One month.,b:Three months.,c:Six months.
note: Under South Carolina's implied consent law, refusal to submit to chemical testing results in a six-month license suspension, in addition to other penalties.

question: How should you scan the road to prepare for hazards?
options: a:Continuously scan the road and roadsides rather than staring straight ahead.,b:Stare straight ahead at all times.,c:Keep your left foot lightly on the brake when scanning.,d:Focus only on the vehicle directly ahead.
note: Safe drivers constantly scan ahead, to the sides, and check mirrors so they can spot hazards early. Looking far down the road and along the roadsides gives you more time to react to braking traffic, pedestrians, or obstacles, instead of staring only straight ahead or at the vehicle directly in front of you.

question: If a vehicle is tailgating you on a two-lane road and you cannot change lanes, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to increase distance between you and the tailgater,b:Slow down gradually to encourage the tailgater to pass,c:Brake sharply to frighten them away,d:Stop in your lane until they pass
note: If you are being tailgated and cannot change lanes, gradually slowing down increases the following distance and often encourages the tailgater to pass when it is safe. Avoid speeding up or braking suddenly, as both can increase the risk of a rear‑end collision.

question: As you approach the crest of a hill, what is the best precaution?
options: a:Maintain the same speed you had earlier.,b:Prepare to stop if necessary.,c:Speed up slightly to clear the hill.
note: When you approach the crest of a hill, you cannot see what is ahead—stopped traffic, a slow vehicle, an animal, or debris may be just over the top. You should ease off the accelerator, cover the brake, and be prepared to stop if necessary. Speeding up reduces your time to react and increases stopping distance, making it more dangerous.

question: Approaching a stopped emergency vehicle with lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Maintain speed and pass closely.,b:Change lanes away from it,c:Drive to the right and stop in the lane next to it.,d:Speed up to get past the scene quickly.
note: If an emergency or roadside assistance vehicle is stopped with lights flashing, change lanes away; if unsafe, slow to below the posted speed and give space.

question: On average, how fast does the body eliminate alcohol?
options: a:Two drinks per hour.,b:Three drinks per hour.,c:About one standard drink per hour.
note: The body typically processes alcohol at an average rate of about one standard drink per hour, though this varies by person based on weight, sex, health, and other factors. Nothing—coffee, cold showers, or exercise—can speed this up; only time reduces your blood alcohol concentration.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their headlights at night, where should you look to avoid being blinded?
options: a:Toward the center of the roadway.,b:Look straight ahead at the lights.,c:Toward the right side of the road.
note: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, do not stare into the bright lights. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road to use the lane line or road edge as a guide. This helps you avoid being blinded while keeping your vehicle in the proper lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway marked with double solid yellow lines, which action is allowed?
options: a:You may not cross them under any circumstance.,b:You may cross only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.,c:You may cross them to pass other vehicles if there is no oncoming traffic.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean passing is prohibited for traffic in both directions. You may not cross them to pass another vehicle. However, you are allowed to cross double solid yellow lines to make a left turn into or from an alley, side street, private road, or driveway when it is safe.

question: What is the purpose of broken yellow lines on the roadway?
options: a:They separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions and indicate passing may be allowed.,b:They separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.,c:They mark pedestrian crosswalks.
note: Broken yellow lines separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions and show that you may pass another vehicle when it is safe and legal to do so. You must still check for oncoming traffic and road conditions before crossing the line.

question: Drowsiness while driving can have effects similar to what other impairments?
options: a:It has no effect on driving ability.,b:It makes you a better driver.,c:It can impair your judgment similar to alcohol and drugs.
note: Drowsy driving slows your reaction time, narrows your attention, and harms your judgment in ways very similar to alcohol or drug impairment. A tired driver may drift from their lane, miss hazards, or react too slowly to avoid a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a four-lane highway, slower traffic should use which lane?
options: a:The right lane.,b:The center lane.,c:Any lane as long as you signal.,d:The left lane.
note: On multi-lane roads, slower traffic should keep right so faster vehicles can pass on the left. The left lane is generally used for passing or faster-moving traffic, which helps traffic flow smoothly and reduces lane-changing conflicts.

question: What does a yellow diamond-shaped sign with black symbols typically indicate?
options: a:Directions to nearby cities and towns,b:Maximum speed limits,c:Traffic laws and regulations,d:A warning about conditions on or near the road ahead
note: Yellow diamond-shaped signs with black symbols are warning signs. They alert you to conditions such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or other hazards so you can slow down and be prepared.

question: What does a broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line mean about passing?
options: a:Passing is prohibited from either direction.,b:Passing is permitted from the side with the broken line and prohibited from the solid line side.,c:Passing is permitted from the side next to the solid line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the broken line, and not allowed for traffic on the side with the solid line. This is used where passing is safe in one direction but too risky in the other.

question: An octagonal road sign always means what?
options: a:Stop.,b:Speed limit.,c:Hospital ahead.
note: An eight‑sided (octagonal) sign is reserved exclusively for STOP signs. When you see this shape, you must come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a heavy truck from behind while going uphill, what should you expect?
options: a:The truck must always pull over to let you pass.,b:You will always be able to safely pass the truck.,c:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit and passing may be unsafe.,d:The truck will always be at posted speed.
note: Large trucks often slow down on upgrades because of their weight, so they may travel below the posted speed limit. On hills, curves, or where visibility is limited, passing can be unsafe or illegal because you may not see oncoming traffic in time. Be patient and only pass where it is legal and you have clear sight distance.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?
options: a:Only when passing another vehicle.,b:When changing lanes.,c:Only when parking.
note: You must check your blind spots by quickly looking over your shoulder whenever you change lanes, merge, or move laterally in traffic, because mirrors do not show every area around your vehicle. A shoulder check helps you see vehicles, motorcycles, bicycles, or pedestrians that may be hidden in your blind spots.

question: Is nighttime the safest time for cyclists to ride?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Nighttime is more dangerous for cyclists because they are harder for drivers to see and depth perception and reaction times are reduced in the dark. Both drivers and bicyclists must use lights and reflectors as required by law and exercise extra caution after dark.

question: When driving near a motorcycle, what must you allow the motorcyclist to use?
options: a:Only half of a lane.,b:A complete lane (full lane width).,c:The shoulder beside the lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, just like any other motor vehicle. Do not crowd a motorcycle or share a lane with it; give the rider the entire lane width so they have room to maneuver around hazards and maintain stability.

question: In fog, rain, or snow, which lights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Fog lights only.
note: In fog, rain, or snow, you should use low-beam headlights because their light aims down toward the road and is less likely to reflect back at you. High beams can bounce off moisture in the air and create glare, making it harder to see.

question: A solid red arrow on a traffic signal means:
options: a:The arrow is only advisory.,b:You may turn if no oncoming traffic is present.,c:Drivers may proceed with caution.,d:The same as a circular red light; do not turn in the arrow's direction.
note: A solid red arrow means you must stop and may not go in the direction of the arrow while it is red. It functions like a circular red light for that specific turning movement: no turns are allowed in that direction until the signal changes or a sign specifically allows a turn on red where permitted by law.

question: What is the only thing that reduces blood alcohol concentration (BAC) and alcohol's effects on the body?
options: a:Eating foods high in fat.,b:Drinking caffeine.,c:Time.
note: Only time lowers your blood alcohol concentration. Your body must metabolize the alcohol, and this process cannot be sped up by food, coffee, cold showers, or exercise. You may feel more awake with caffeine, but you will still be impaired until enough time has passed.

question: True or False: Your driving speed has no effect on the distance your vehicle travels after you apply the brakes.
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE,c:Only on dry roads,d:Only with ABS brakes
note: Speed has a major effect on stopping distance. The faster you drive, the longer it takes to react and the farther your vehicle travels after you hit the brakes. Both reaction distance and braking distance increase with speed, so higher speeds require much more space to stop safely.

question: When passing a row of parked vehicles, what should you be prepared for?
options: a:Assume parked cars will stay stationary,b:Driving closely to parked vehicles to allow more room for traffic,c:A person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane,d:Other drivers and pedestrians will always observe the right-of-way
note: When passing parked vehicles, you should expect that a car door might open, a vehicle might pull out, or a pedestrian might step into your lane. Slow down if needed, leave extra space, and be ready to brake or steer smoothly to avoid sudden hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Only pedestrians may proceed.,b:You may drive through the intersection if the way is clear and may turn unless prohibited,c:You must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.,d:Slow down and prepare to stop.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn, if it is not prohibited by signs or signals, but only if the intersection is clear. You must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Another driver is attempting to pass your vehicle. What should you do?
options: a:Pull off the road,b:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing,c:Signal to the other driver when it is safe for them to pass,d:Speed up to prevent them from passing
note: When another driver is passing you, stay in your lane, maintain a steady speed, or slightly reduce speed if needed so they can pass and return safely. Do not speed up or signal them when to pass; simply make it easier and safer for them to complete the maneuver.

question: What do pentagonal road signs indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:Speed limits.,c:School zones and school crossings.,d:General warning signs.
note: Pentagonal (five-sided) signs are used for school zones and school crossings. When you see this shape, slow down, watch carefully for children, and be prepared to stop for pedestrians in or approaching the crosswalk.

question: Traffic signs with an orange background typically warn of:
options: a:School zones.,b:General roadway hazards.,c:Regulatory rules.,d:Construction and maintenance work.
note: Orange traffic signs are used for temporary traffic control in construction and maintenance areas. They warn you of road work, lane shifts, workers, and equipment so you can slow down, follow directions, and drive with extra caution.

question: A flashing yellow traffic light indicates drivers should:
options: a:Yield only to pedestrians.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Stop and wait for green.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down and proceed with extra caution. Look for cross traffic, pedestrians, and other hazards, and be prepared to yield if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you begin a left turn from multilane, one-way streets?
options: a:The middle of the intersection.,b:The right lane.,c:The left lane.
note: On a multilane, one‑way street, you must begin a left turn from the leftmost lane that is designated for left turns. Starting from the correct lane keeps you aligned with traffic and prevents cutting across other lanes during the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate highway from a ramp, what should you do?
options: a:Use the ramp and acceleration lane to match freeway speed, check traffic, and merge into a safe gap.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp and enter when it feels safe.,c:Slow to well below freeway speed so other drivers can adjust.
note: When entering an interstate, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, check mirrors and blind spots, and merge when there is a safe gap. You should not stop at the end of the ramp unless traffic or signals require it, because stopping makes merging dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Only when there is a stop sign.,b:Whenever a police officer orders you to stop.,c:At a steady or flashing red traffic light.,d:Both b and c.
note: You must stop whenever a police officer directs you to and at steady or flashing red traffic lights, as well as at stop signs and certain other situations. Traffic control devices and lawful orders from officers must always be obeyed.

question: Before driving after taking medication, what should you do?
options: a:Double your following distance only at night.,b:Make more rest stops than usual.,c:Drive immediately so the medicine won't affect you.,d:Understand the medication's effects and adjust your driving.
note: Many prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines can make you drowsy, dizzy, or slow your reactions. Always read the label or ask a doctor or pharmacist how the medication may affect driving, and avoid driving if it can impair your alertness, coordination, or judgment.

question: When sharing the road with bicyclists, you should do which of the following?
options: a:Treat bicycles as vehicles on the road and be extra careful when near them.,b:Pass as closely as possible because they're small.,c:Expect them to always yield to you.
note: Bicycles are vehicles and usually have the same rights and duties as drivers. Give cyclists extra space, pass only when it is safe, and never crowd them. Leave a wide clearance when passing and be careful not to turn across their path after you pass.

question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line indicates what?
options: a:Vehicles next to the broken line may pass when safe.,b:Vehicles in both directions may pass anytime.,c:Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.
note: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means only the vehicles on the side with the broken line are allowed to pass, and only when it is safe. Vehicles on the side with the solid yellow line must not cross it to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at a 4-way stop at the same time as a driver on your left. Who has the right of way?
options: a:The driver on your left, because they were there first,b:You have the right of way — the driver to your left must yield to you,c:Whoever signals first proceeds first,d:The driver going straight always has priority
note: At a 4-way stop when two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver to the RIGHT has the right of way. Since the other driver is to your LEFT, you are to their right — meaning you have the right of way and should proceed first.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Get out of your vehicle and flag down the first vehicle that passes.,b:Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle, if you can.,c:Sound your horn at passing cars to get their attention.
note: If you must stop on an interstate, pull completely off the travel lanes onto the shoulder if possible, turn on your emergency flashers so others can see you, and stay inside your vehicle with your seat belt fastened unless there is an immediate danger such as fire or traffic striking your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to pass on a two-lane road, what should be your primary check?
options: a:Judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles.,b:Flash your headlights as you pass.,c:Sound your horn as you pass.,d:Assume oncoming traffic will slow down.
note: Before passing on a two-lane road, your main concern is whether there is enough clear space ahead in the oncoming lane. Carefully judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles and only begin passing if you are sure you can complete the maneuver and return to your lane without forcing any other driver to slow or swerve.

question: On which road marking may you legally pass another vehicle?
options: a:You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,b:You are on a hill or curve.,c:You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
note: A broken center line next to your lane means you may pass when it is safe. A solid line next to your lane means you must not pass, and you should never pass on hills, curves, or anywhere your view of oncoming traffic is limited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, you should move back into your original lane when:
options: a:You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,b:You can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.,d:The passing vehicle signals you to move over.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until you can see the front of the vehicle you passed (its headlights in the daytime or at night) in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead and do not cut off the other driver.

question: What do blue traffic signs generally indicate?
options: a:Regulatory requirements like speed limits.,b:Mileage distances to locations.,c:Construction and maintenance warnings.,d:Information on motorist services (rest areas, hospitals, food).
note: Blue traffic signs are service signs. They give information about motorist services such as rest areas, gas stations, food, lodging, and hospitals along the roadway.

question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic to merge safely?
options: a:Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.,b:Using only your rearview mirror.,c:Using your rearview and side mirrors without looking over your shoulder.
note: Before merging onto a freeway, use your mirrors and then look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This helps you see vehicles that are not visible in your mirrors so you can choose a safe gap and merge smoothly.

question: If a child is about to run into the street, what should you do?
options: a:Sound a sharp blast of your horn while being prepared to stop.,b:Flash your headlights.,c:Continue at the same speed.
note: If a child appears ready to run into the street, immediately cover the brake and be prepared to stop while giving a sharp blast of your horn to warn the child and others nearby. Use the horn to alert, but your primary responsibility is to slow or stop to avoid a collision.

question: What must you do when approaching a pedestrian who uses a guide dog or white cane?
options: a:Honk so they know to clear the way.,b:Swerve quickly around them.,c:Yield the right-of-way.
note: Stop and give the blind pedestrian the right-of-way; do not honk or attempt to steer around them abruptly.

question: Any amount of alcohol in your blood may affect which abilities?
options: a:Right-of-way privileges.,b:Judgment and physical coordination.,c:Knowledge.
note: Any amount of alcohol can affect your judgment and physical coordination, even if you do not feel drunk. Because driving requires quick decisions and precise control, even small amounts of alcohol can make driving unsafe.
